# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC is weighing a twenty percent CoWoS price hike as packaging stays tight.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC is weighing a twenty percent price increase on CoWoS while AI demand keeps advanced packaging tight. Intel is pulling 18A wafers off Panther Lake so it can build more Granite Rapids. A 700-megawatt data centre is proposed outside Lansing, and SpaceX is reported to be buying 418 nearby homes only if owners drop a lawsuit.

### Top Story
Semiconductor Engineering’s week in review says TSMC is considering a 20 percent price increase for CoWoS as AI demand continues to strain advanced-packaging capacity. The same review says ASE forecasts a doubling of its advanced-packaging revenue in 2027. Amkor is ramping new high-density fan-out and 2.5D packaging programs. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-162/)

### Silicon
**Intel pulls Panther Lake wafers for Granite Rapids: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware reports that Intel is taking 18A wafers that had been going to Panther Lake offline, freeing that capacity so Oregon can put Intel 3 in and build more Granite Rapids data-centre CPUs. Nova Lake, already on the client roadmap, is now confirmed by CEO Lip-Bu Tan as the first 18A-P client product and is tracking ahead of schedule. Design wins at launch are expected to be twice those of Panther Lake, with more detail at CES in January. Against 18A, 18A-P is a 9 percent speed gain at the same power, or an 18 percent power cut at the same speed, and Intel has described it as a drop-in for 18A designs. Demand for Wildcat Lake is outstripping supply. Intel expects its client business to decline by more than 20 percent next quarter, and the 2026 PC-unit market to decline about 12 percent. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/intel-confirms-nova-lake-will-use-advanced-18a-p-node-more-details-at-ces-company-says-its-taking-panther-lake-capacity-offline-to-build-more-granite-rapids-data-center-cpus)

**SK hynix creates a US Americas chief post: BigGo Finance**
SK hynix has created a president-level Americas organization based in the United States and named development chief Ahn Hyun to lead it, effective November 1. Ahn has led AI memory development, including HBM and SOCAMM. The role is to build a response system around US big-tech customers and to strengthen technology leadership and R&D. Cha Sun-yong takes the development post while continuing as head of the Future Technology Research Institute. Yoon Poong-young moves to head the Corporate Center, and CEO Kwak Noh-jung stays after six consecutive record quarters. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/bfcad863-99fa-46ae-ab33-c71c149458e5)

**Hanmi Semiconductor receives an SK hynix plaque: Chosunbiz**
Hanmi Semiconductor said on October 30 that it received a plaque from SK hynix for HBM equipment and mass-production support. The companies have worked together since a 2015 thermocompression bonder, and cumulative equipment sales to SK hynix over ten years are about 600 billion won. In 2017 Hanmi developed Korea’s first dual TC bonder, which it says roughly doubled productivity versus earlier tools, and the two companies jointly won the IR52 Jang Young Sil Award. TC bonders have supported SK hynix from HBM2 through HBM3, HBM3E and HBM4, including HBM supplied to NVIDIA. Hanmi runs offices in Cheongju and Icheon and a Silver Phoenix support team with 30 vehicles. Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-it/2026/10/30/372GBYGCXBHK3OTEQ7YSIR6OLA/)

**FuriosaAI closes a $620 million Series D: HPCwire**
FuriosaAI said it completed a $620 million Series D to scale production of its data-centre AI inference accelerator and to accelerate next-generation silicon. Investors named in the announcement include Infinitum, Jericho Capital, QUDA Capital, Cisco Investments, Worldline Capital, the National Growth Fund of Korea and Korean institutions. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/furiosaai-secures-620m-series-d-to-meet-ai-inference-demand-and-accelerate-next-gen-silicon/)

**BrainChip launches an AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 kit: HPCwire**
BrainChip’s AKD1500 Raspberry Pi 5 Development Kit is available now through the BrainChip Shop. It pairs a Raspberry Pi 5 with the AKD1500 M.2 board so teams can evaluate the same chip they would design in, using PCIe or SPI. The chip is event-based, processes on the device, and supports on-chip learning of new classes without a cloud retrain. MetaTF tools and models are free through the BrainChip Developer Hub. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/brainchip-launches-akd1500-raspberry-pi-5-kit/)

**C Sun subscribes for a Nemstek stake: digitimes**
C Sun Manufacturing said on October 30 that it would subscribe for 1,900 lots of Nemstek’s privately placed common shares as a strategic investor. The expected stake on completion is about 4.68 percent, aimed at expanding advanced-packaging equipment. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261030PD235/equipment-packaging-investment-automation-technology.html)

### Data Centres & Power
**700MW data center project proposed outside Lansing: Data Center Dynamics**
A 700-megawatt data-centre project is announced outside Lansing, Michigan. Data Center Dynamics reports that local officials were blindsided by a proposal from the local economic development agency. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/700mw-data-center-project-proposed-outside-lansing-michigan/)

**SpaceX buyout of homes near an AI data centre: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware reports that SpaceX is buying out 418 homes near a flagship AI data centre, and only from owners who drop participation in a lawsuit. The properties are supposed to house SpaceXSI staff and to give neighbours who do not want to live beside the data centre a way to sell. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/elon-musks-spacex-buying-out-418-homes-near-flagship-ai-data-center-but-only-if-they-drop-participation-in-lawsuit-report-claims-the-company-is-targeting-an-entire-neighborhood-but-will-only-buy-from-people-who-dont-pursue-noise-pollution-complaints)

**Heim secures Omnes investment for Finland: Data Center Dynamics**
Nordic data-centre firm Heim has secured an investment from Omnes. The investment is to fund Heim’s first projects in Finland. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nordic-data-center-firm-heim-secures-investment-from-omnes/)

**Quantum DC cancels an Australian community meeting: Data Center Dynamics**
Quantum DC’s Australian project is announced at gigawatt scale and has drawn local pushback. The company cancelled a community meeting after what it called a credible bomb threat. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/quantum-dc-cancels-australian-data-center-community-meeting-over-credible-bomb-threat/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**CXMT plans limited HBM3E production: Semiconductor Engineering**
China’s CXMT plans to begin limited production of HBM3E soon, Semiconductor Engineering reports, citing Reuters. Manufacturing yields are put at 20 to 30 percent. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-162/)

**Vietnam’s first fab may miss a 2027 trial: Semiconductor Engineering**
Vietnam’s first semiconductor fab may miss its 2027 trial-production target, according to Reuters as carried by Semiconductor Engineering. The estimated $1.3 billion Viettel project reportedly has yet to begin construction, and talks for ASML lithography tools remain unresolved. Viettel says the project is on schedule. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-162/)

**PCB shortages projected out to 2030: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp, citing Nikkei Asia, says PCB shortages are projected to last until 2030. An unnamed executive at an American PC maker said some manufacturers expect orders placed today not to be fulfilled until late 2028, and that PCB supply is still short even if PC shipments fall again next year. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354289/motherboard-and-gpu-prices-could-rise-further-as-pcb-shortages-extend-to-2030)

**TANAKA and MEP form a Penang refining venture: Semiconductor Digest**
TANAKA and MEP are establishing a precious-metal refining joint venture in Batu Kawan Industrial Park, Penang, Malaysia. TANAKA will hold 66.7 percent and MEP 33.3 percent. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/tanaka-and-mep-to-establish-precious-metal-refining-joint-venture-in-malaysia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=tanaka-and-mep-to-establish-precious-metal-refining-joint-venture-in-malaysia)

### Also Today
**IQM reports full-chip entanglement on 54 qubits: HPCwire**
IQM said its cloud-accessible Emerald system has fully entangled all 54 qubits on the chip at once, with fidelity held above the entanglement threshold. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/iqm-reports-full-chip-entanglement-on-54-qubit-quantum-processor/)

**Nagare Labs emerges with $5 million: Semiconductor Digest**
Atlanta spinout Nagare Labs raised $5 million from Playground Global to build a new memory tier aimed at AI’s memory bottleneck. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/nagare-labs-emerges-from-stealth-to-break-ais-memory-bottleneck/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=nagare-labs-emerges-from-stealth-to-break-ais-memory-bottleneck)

### The Teardown: When the Night Shift Does Not Buy a Node
A process node does not move because the lab stays lit. It moves when someone can still tell a real signal from a measurement artefact, and that judgment does not stack the way wafer starts do. Wccftech’s account of TSMC co-COO and executive vice president Y.P. Chyn, speaking to students at National Cheng Kung University, is a rare on-the-record demolition of the hours theory of research.

The mechanism is simple once you separate the fab clock from the research clock. A production line gains output when a second shift loads more lots onto tools that already have a qualified recipe. Lithography, etch and deposition do not need the same engineer to be awake for every wafer. Development does. A new module is a chain of hypotheses: which film, which dose, which anneal, which defect is the limiter. The next experiment is only useful if the last one was interpreted. If the interpretation is wrong, the night crew does not buy time. It buys a second pile of wafers aimed at the wrong variable. Chyn’s line, as reported, is that research runs on brainpower, not labour, and that longer hours do not by themselves produce the result.

The worked example is the Night Owl program, from a period when TSMC was behind on process technology and trying to catch competitors. The theory inside the company was arithmetic. If TSMC’s research team worked 24 hours a day and US competitors worked only eight, TSMC would hold a time advantage and could overtake them. Twenty-four divided by eight is three. Three times the staffed hours, on that theory, should have been three times the learning rate. TSMC encouraged research engineers to take night development work so the organization would stay open around the clock. The plan was declared a failure within six months, half a year. The multiplier never showed up in the node. The missing term in the arithmetic was decision quality per hour, not hours per day. A tired team running the same mis-specified split does not converge faster. It converges on noise, and the morning team spends the next day unwinding it. That is why a 3x hours claim collapsed inside six months instead of compounding.

Chyn put the organizational repair at the 40-nanometre node. The old sequence was research finishes a process, then hands it to the fab. That handoff hit serious setbacks. The replacement, which TSMC calls One Team, is not a slogan about helping. It is shared ownership of the final result across departments. He gave two examples. First, when a new process moves from research into volume production, a longer overlap, with the fab in the development early, makes the ramp smoother. Second, when a fab hits a process problem, several teams on the root cause resolve it faster than one unit isolating the fault alone. The same rule is what he applies to fabs outside Taiwan: they cannot run as organizations fully cut off from Taiwan, and Taiwan teams have to carry some of the result. He also said getting departments to actually take that shared accountability takes a great deal of time and cannot be done with slogans.

The design choice stops being the right one when the work really is lot-limited rather than judgment-limited. A qualified recipe on a production tool, with the split already decided and the metrology already trusted, does gain from a second shift. Night Owl was the opposite case: an open research problem treated as if it were a loading problem. The moment the next wafer’s value depends on an interpretation that has not been made, adding the other sixteen hours of the day does not finish the node. It only keeps the lights on while the hypothesis stays wrong. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/tsmc-co-coo-chyn-longer-hours-dont-improve-rd-night-owl-program-failed/)

### On the Horizon
: Ahn Hyun’s Americas role at SK hynix takes effect.
- January 2027: Intel expects to share more on Nova Lake at CES.
- Late 2028: some PCB makers, via Nikkei, do not expect today’s orders filled before then, with tightness projected toward 2030.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Nineteen point two terabytes per second is the Vera Rubin bandwidth buyers get, not twenty-two.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia’s production Vera Rubin sheet sustains 19.2 terabytes per second of HBM4, under the 22 terabytes per second development target. Nvidia and AMD are putting a combined $4 billion into Meta as that company raises equity for AI infrastructure. AUO’s board has approved a NT$38.8 billion sale of a Taichung plant to TSMC and killed a smaller Quanta disposal.

### Top Story
Nvidia told Wccftech that specifications published during Vera Rubin’s development were preliminary architectural targets, and that the figures now on nvidia.com and the Vera Rubin datasheet are what the system sustains at qualified, volume production. HBM4 bandwidth on that sheet is 19.2 terabytes per second, against 22 terabytes per second at unveiling, which Wccftech calculates as 12.7 percent lower; sixth-generation NVLink is 3 terabytes per second, against 3.6, a 16.7 percent cut, and both cuts apply to NVL72 and NVL8. Each Rubin GPU had been shown with 288 gigabytes of HBM4. Yesterday’s Oracle availability was these production systems; what moved is the bandwidth Nvidia now prints for them. Nvidia said Vera Rubin NVL72 is in full production and shipping, that third-party agentic benchmarks already used those production specifications, and that those measurements show 30 times the performance per watt and 30 times the tokens per dollar versus the prior GB300 NVL72. The company said individual component specifications do not determine application performance for agent workloads, which it described as decided at data-centre scale. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/nvidia-official-statement-on-vera-rubin-spec-change/)

### Silicon
**Nvidia, AMD Commit $4B to Meta AI Buildout: Data Center Knowledge**
Nvidia and AMD are investing a combined $4 billion in Meta, Nvidia $3 billion and AMD $1 billion, after Meta disclosed on October 26 that it plans to raise $97.5 billion in an equity offering for AI infrastructure. Nvidia’s investment was announced the same day; AMD’s followed on Tuesday. Meta plans to deploy more Nvidia infrastructure, including the Vera Rubin platform, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and BlueField-4 DPUs. AMD said initial Helios rack-scale systems have been installed and are being tested by Meta ahead of a broader deployment. AMD also said Meta has deployed millions of Epyc processors, is a lead customer of sixth-generation Epyc, uses Instinct GPUs for training, ranking, and recommendation, and plans a custom Instinct GPU for its own workloads. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-chips/nvidia-amd-commit-4b-to-meta-ai-buildout)

**TSMC To Commence A14 Process Node Mass Production in the First Half of 2028: Wccftech**
DigiTimes, as reported by Wccftech, says TSMC’s A14 node is set for risk production in the second half of 2027 and mass production in the first half of 2028, with Hsinchu Science Park Baoshan Fab 20 and Central Taiwan Science Park Fab 25 as the primary sites. The same report says A14 capacity in 2028 will be 7.5 times Intel’s 14A capacity. Wccftech reports A14 at 15 percent higher speed at the same power, up to 30 percent better power efficiency, and up to 20 percent density versus N2, using second-generation gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and NanoFlex Pro. ETNews, cited there, says A14 is the node that scales the SRAM bit cell from 0.021 square micrometres to 0.017, and that TSMC will announce research results by year-end on a cell under 0.017 square micrometres. Intel’s 18A, already in volume production, is described with a 0.021-square-micrometre high-density cell and up to 38.1 megabits per square millimetre, matching the 2-nanometre SRAM figures Wccftech quotes for TSMC. Cadence locked TSMC A14 tool certification last month, which Wccftech says cuts design-iteration time by 2.5 times. Pilot production of A14 is reported as started. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/tsmc-a14-process-node-mass-production-first-half-2028-7-5x-capacity-intel-14a/)

**Intel Readies Moon Lake and Wildcat Lake Refresh Built on 18A Node: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp reports that Intel is preparing Moon Lake, a low-power SoC with no performance cores and up to four Darkmont low-power-efficiency cores on an 18A die, a reported 6-watt base power, and the BGA1516 package already used by Wildcat Lake. The reported codename is MNL, aimed at embedded devices such as network-attached storage, and described as a possible successor to the N-series. A Wildcat Lake Refresh is reported to raise performance cores from two to four, keep four Darkmont cores and up to two Xe3 graphics cores, and add vPro. The Core 300 Wildcat Lake parts launched earlier this year are described with up to two performance cores, four efficiency cores, up to two Xe3 cores, and a package reaching 35 watts. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354255/intel-readies-moon-lake-and-wildcat-lake-refresh-built-on-18a-node)

**Oracle expands NVIDIA AI cloud with Vera Rubin systems: DataCenterNews Asia Pacific**
Oracle plans to introduce NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8, an eight-GPU system in an x86 server with two 64-core Intel Xeon 6 processors, 4 terabytes of DDR5, and 6.4 terabits per second of RDMA networking, for customers who want Rubin GPUs in a smaller configuration than NVL72. In Abilene, OpenAI has trained and served GPT-6 Astra on an OCI Supercluster with more than 100,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs. OpenAI is also testing Vera CPUs on OCI for agentic sandbox workloads. Source: [datacenternews.asia](https://datacenternews.asia/story/oracle-expands-nvidia-ai-cloud-with-vera-rubin-systems)

### Data Centres & Power
**Tata Communications to invest $450m into 10,000km of AI-ready fiber to support data center connectivity in India: Data Center Dynamics**
Tata Communications is investing $450 million in 10,000 kilometres of AI-ready fibre to support data-centre connectivity in India. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/tata-communications-to-invest-450m-into-10000km-of-ai-ready-fiber-to-support-data-center-connectivity-in-india/)

**KBRA assigns preliminary ratings to up to $525m in US Signal notes, secured against ten data centers: Data Center Dynamics**
KBRA has assigned preliminary ratings to up to $525 million of US Signal notes secured against ten data centres, with a final maturity of November 2056. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/kbra-assigns-preliminary-ratings-to-up-to-525m-in-us-signal-notes-secured-against-ten-data-centers/)

**Cowboy Space Unveils Big Iron Rocket Designed to Become an Orbital Data Center: HPCwire**
Cowboy Space, the San Carlos company founded by Baiju Bhatt, has unveiled a rocket architecture meant to put compute in orbit and to carry more than 15,000 kilograms per launch, including third-party payloads. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/cowboy-space-unveils-big-iron-rocket-designed-to-become-an-orbital-data-center/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**AUO sells Taichung plant to TSMC for NT$38.8B, scraps Quanta deal: digitimes**
AUO’s board has approved the sale of its Taichung Plant Phase II facilities and related infrastructure to TSMC for NT$38.8 billion, about $1.2 billion, excluding taxes. BigGo Finance puts the site in the Anlin section of Xitun District, Taichung, covering a Gen 5 fab and a Gen 7.5 fab, with a registered area of about 129,700 ping, roughly 428,000 square metres, and an estimated disposal gain of about NT$18.5 billion, or about $568.7 million. A planned NT$19.7 billion sale of Huaya facilities to Quanta has been terminated; BigGo Finance says the sides could not agree on plant-usage specifications and delivery timelines. The same earnings call reported a third-quarter basic loss of NT$0.33 per share. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261029PD237/auo-tsmc-plant-infrastructure-development.html) Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/0e2245e3-5b15-4217-b523-398361d5ad9f)

**Taiwan's Eternal Materials Posts NT$388 Million September Pretax Profit: BigGo Finance**
Eternal Materials reported September pretax profit of NT$388 million, about $11.9 million, up 158.28 percent from a year earlier. Semiconductor advanced-packaging materials and precision equipment both set monthly revenue records; packaging-material shipments are now contributing to profit, and precision equipment is in intensive customer acceptance testing, with revenue expected to climb further. September consolidated revenue was NT$4.433 billion, about $136.4 million, a 51-month high. The company expects fourth-quarter demand across its three major lines to extend third-quarter peak-season momentum, and it flagged an unclear Middle East situation and raw-material price volatility. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/6c12b5a9-40b3-49a0-b9f9-4b25057c86a6)

**Lam and imec Expand Collaboration to Advance Manufacturability of Next-Gen 3D Integration Technologies: Semiconductor Digest**
Lam has extended its collaboration with imec to two new joint development focuses: manufacturability of advanced 3D integration, and Aether dry resist for future high-NA EUV patterning. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/lam-and-imec-expand-collaboration-to-advance-manufacturability-of-next-gen-3d-integration-technologies/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=lam-and-imec-expand-collaboration-to-advance-manufacturability-of-next-gen-3d-integration-technologies)

**The EU Cyber Resilience Act Reaches Chip And IP Suppliers: Semiconductor Engineering**
The Cyber Resilience Act’s mandatory reporting phase took effect in September 2026: an early warning when a vulnerability is being exploited or a severe incident hits security, then a fuller notification and a final report, filed through the Single Reporting Platform. The regulation applies to semiconductors sold separately, and it lists microprocessors, microcontrollers, ASICs, and FPGAs. Broader cybersecurity, conformity-assessment, and documentation duties, plus CE marking, take effect on December 11, 2027. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/the-eu-cyber-resilience-act-reaches-chip-and-ip-suppliers/)

### Also Today
**Samsung boosts HBM4 to 60% of HBM sales as SK hynix narrows gap: Chosunbiz**
Samsung has raised HBM4 to 60 percent of its HBM sales while SK hynix narrows the gap. Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-it/2026/10/29/RPHAESD7IZBJ5IKBEIM45P6CCQ/)

**Georgia's Utility Board Race Could Reshape Nearly 20 GW Pipeline Of Data Centers: Bisnow**
A Georgia utility-board race could reshape a data-centre pipeline of nearly 20 gigawatts. Source: [bisnow.com](https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/data-center/georgia-utility-board-race-could-reshape-nearly-20-gigawatt-data-center-pipeline)

**Jülich Gets Sparse Computing Boost from Sparxity Accelerators: HPCwire**
The Jülich Supercomputing Centre has tapped Sparxity, formerly SpiNNcloud, for sparse workloads that fit GPUs poorly. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/28/julich-gets-sparse-computing-boost-from-sparxity-accelerators/)

### The Teardown: The Solver Signs the Stage
Every autonomous step in a chip flow is either inside the physics or it is a risk the next step inherits. Semiconductor Engineering carries a Siemens account of what that means once agents drive electronic design automation. A self-verifying agent can inspect its own work. A physics-validated workflow is the stricter object: every agent decision is confirmed against a deterministic, physics-based engine before the next step begins. The engine, not the model, is the authority on correctness. Tapeout does not grade on a curve. Silicon works or it does not, and a model that can discuss heat or timing does not relax that binary.

The check cannot wait for the end of the run, because misses compound. A workflow that reasons about physics and does not validate outputs against those engines adds risk at every autonomous step. The longer it runs without validation, the further a design can drift before an error surfaces. Across multiple tools, multiple physical domains, and hours without a person in the loop, unvalidated decisions stack. Continuous validation is what keeps an early miss from becoming the assumption the next tool is built on.

Three-dimensional integrated circuits are the case the account uses. Stacked active dies make heat removal and temperature interactions harder to predict, and the package can add mechanical stress. Electrical, power, thermal, and mechanical effects are tied together, so a change in one moves the others. Doing that by hand, tool by tool, creates engineering handoffs, slows iteration, and caps how many alternatives a team can try. AI factories, the piece notes, are asking for more compute, memory bandwidth, and thermal performance inside a tighter footprint, which is why chiplet 2.5D and 3D packages are carrying the scaling once a monolithic die runs out of room.

The worked example is a nine-stage electro-thermal workflow. MCP servers and skill files for the tools connect to Fuse, which aggregates them, and in this example Claude Code is the coding agent. The flow spans seven Siemens EDA tools and runs 100 to 200 agentic turns over more than 12 hours. Stages run from floor planning, library characterization, and power analysis through thermal signoff, system-level thermal simulation, parasitic extraction, and power- and temperature-aware SPICE simulation. Each stage is validated with signoff-grade physics solvers. The agent executes, reads the result, and keeps refining when a target is missed. It does not bank a stage and hope a final signoff catches it.

The sweep is what those hours are for. Teams can vary heat-transfer-coefficient boundaries, power budgets, and material stack-ups across 200 to 500 or more design points in a cycle. Five hundred divided by two hundred is 2.5, so the top of that stated range is two and a half times the bottom, inside one cycle. The account says the same machinery lets teams configure tools up to 20 times faster, cut engineering effort by up to 95 percent, and evaluate up to 50 times more design options than a conventional manual flow. The 20-times configuration speed is what makes a run of more than 12 hours and 100 to 200 turns able to touch hundreds of points instead of a handful of hand-built decks. The 50-times claim and the 200-to-500 point range are the article’s own measures of that wider search, not two labs reporting the same experiment.

This control stops being the right one when a stage is allowed to advance because the agent is satisfied and the solver speaks only after the twelve hours. At that point a search up to 50 times wider than a manual flow is also up to 50 times more ways for an early, unvalidated miss to propagate through seven tools, and the binary tapeout check arrives after the drift has already been designed in. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/physics-based-validation-the-foundation-of-trustworthy-agentic-eda/)

### On the Horizon
- TSMC is to announce A14 SRAM research results, including a bit cell under 0.017 square micrometres, by the end of 2026.
- A14 risk production is reported for the second half of 2027, with mass production in the first half of 2028 at Fab 20 and Fab 25.
- The Cyber Resilience Act’s broader conformity, documentation, and CE-marking duties take effect on December 11, 2027.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Seventy-two-GPU Vera Rubin racks are live on Oracle Cloud at multi-gigawatt scale.**

**What You Need to Know:** Seventy-two-GPU Vera Rubin NVL72 racks are generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and Oracle and NVIDIA say OCI Superclusters on that platform will expand to multi-gigawatt scale. NVIDIA Vera CPUs are generally available on the same cloud, with an x86 Rubin server still only on the plan. Memory makers, meanwhile, are booking capacity years out while a Chinese HBM3E line is still fighting yield.

### Top Story
NVIDIA and Oracle say Vera Rubin NVL72 and NVIDIA Vera CPUs are generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as of 27 October 2026, and they plan to expand OCI Superclusters built on NVL72 to multi-gigawatt scale. That expansion is a plan, not an energized multi-gigawatt site. Each rack links 72 GPUs through NVLink; OCI Superclusters combine those racks with Oracle Acceleron networking, NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet, Spectrum-6 switches and BlueField-4 DPUs, and gigawatt-class power and cooling, with OCI’s multiplanar network described as extending across hundreds of thousands of GPUs. The estate already includes GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems. OCI also plans an x86 HGX Rubin NVL8 with eight Rubin GPUs on NVLink, two 64-core Intel Xeon 6 CPUs, 4TB of DDR5 and 6.4 Tbps of RDMA networking. Tom's Hardware reports this as NVIDIA’s first standalone CPU push at a hyperscaler — OCI’s other Arm instance has been Ampere Altra — and says NVIDIA has put Vera memory bandwidth at 1.2 terabytes per second on LPDDR5X-9600. In Tom's Hardware’s own Stream triad test, not run on OCI, that system more than doubled a dual Intel Xeon 6980P server using MRDIMMs at 8,800 MT/s. In Abilene, Texas, OpenAI has already trained and served on an OCI Supercluster with more than 100,000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Google Cloud announced general availability for Vera Rubin last week. Source: [datacentremagazine.com](https://datacentremagazine.com/news/nvidia-and-oracle-take-vera-rubin-to-multi-gigawatt-scale)
Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/nvidia-and-oracle-bring-vera-cpu-instances-online-in-multi-gigawatt-deployment-oci-superclusters-also-set-to-expand-with-rubin-only-clusters-attached-to-dual-xeon-6-hosts)

### Silicon
**SK Hynix reports record quarter and books memory through 2029: EE Times**
SK Hynix posted third-quarter revenue of 104.62 trillion won, about $78 billion, operating profit of 83.33 trillion won, about $62 billion, and an operating margin of 80 percent. Net profit was 39.78 trillion won, about $30 billion, and net cash expanded to 98.7 trillion won, about $74 billion. Counterpoint’s MS Hwang said operating profit beat a 77 trillion won consensus, about $57 billion, and that standard DRAM pricing has moved from 20 to 30 cents per gigabit to $2 per gigabit, with the global DRAM market at $200 billion on Counterpoint’s count. He argued HBM4 unit price could reach $4 per gigabit, and said October has resolved worries that SK Hynix could not supply HBM4 to NVIDIA and that HBM volume per chip might fall. TechPowerUp reports average selling prices in the quarter rose more than 20 percent from the prior quarter. Digitimes reports the company says customers want more than twice the HBM it can supply. Korea JoongAng Daily reports DRAM and HBM booked through 2029. The company expects demand to outpace supply through 2030, citing 10-nanometre-class sixth-generation DRAM and 321-layer NAND, and says long-term agreements with 14 tech giants cover more than half of capacity for 2027 and 2028. Counterpoint expects Samsung to lead HBM share from the HBM4 generation in 2027; SK Hynix says proprietary packaging and customer partnerships will keep its lead. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/sk-hynix-reports-record-q3-results-driven-by-ai-memory-surge/)
Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261028VL222/sk-hynix-hbm-dram-hbm4-manufacturing.html)
Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354215/sk-hynix-expects-memory-demand-to-outpace-supply-through-2030)
Source: [koreajoongangdaily.com](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/sk-hynix-says-dram-hbm-booked-through-2029-as-profit-soars-to-62b/12942008)

**CXMT to start HBM3E mass production by the end of 2026: TechPowerUp**
Reuters reports CXMT is expected to start mass production of its first HBM, in HBM3E, within two months, by the end of 2026. Risk production began in August, and yields are still a problem. TechPowerUp says it does not have CXMT performance figures, and cites JEDEC’s HBM3E envelope instead: 1,024-bit width, 9.2 to 12.4 gigabits per second per pin, with most standard configurations at 9.6, about 1.2 terabytes per second, and 24 GB in an 8-high stack or 36 GB in a 12-high stack of 24-gigabit layers. Front-end yield is described at around 30 percent, with back-end processing adding about 70 percent on top of that 30 percent. The report says CXMT is attempting HBM3E with about 3,000 through-silicon vias per layer, against about 5,000 per layer Samsung has used on HBM2 and more than 8,000 SK hynix has used on HBM3, in an 8-high stack, and is unlikely to move to 12-high soon. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354226/cxmt-to-start-hbm3e-mass-production-by-the-end-of-2026)

**Intel's Lip-Bu Tan discusses possible AMD cooperation and foundry timing: TechPowerUp**
At an October 24 fireside chat with Jimmy Cheng of the Chinese American Semiconductor Professional Association, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said he has spoken with AMD CEO Lisa Su about possible cooperation. AMD was earlier reported to be evaluating Intel’s 14A node. TechPowerUp reports 18A is in volume production, while 14A has its 0.5 process design kit out, with 0.9 next and 1.0 aimed at volume production early next year. Intel had targeted October for handing the 0.9 kit to outside customers; Tan’s stay-tuned line is read as meaning that handoff has not happened. He said Intel has to reclaim CPU leadership and will tailor chips such as Xeon to customers. He named ASICs, co-packaged optics, physical AI and advanced packaging as growth areas, and wants two or three of them to reach about 10 percent of Intel revenue each. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354221/intels-lip-bu-tan-discusses-possible-amd-cooperation-lays-out-cpu-and-foundry-plans)

### Data Centres & Power
**Nebul to deploy over 1,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in Belgium: Techzine Global**
Nebul says it will deploy more than 1,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in Belgium. That is a deployment plan, not a figure for site power. Source: [techzine.eu](https://www.techzine.eu/news/infrastructure/145360/nebul-to-deploy-over-1000-blackwell-ultra-gpus-in-belgium/)

**US Signal acquires a Hillsboro data center previously occupied by Oracle: Data Center Dynamics**
US Signal has acquired a data center in Hillsboro, Oregon, previously occupied by Oracle. The report does not treat the deal as a new build. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/us-signal-acquires-data-center-in-hillsboro-oregon/)

**Enphase and Infineon deploy 900V GaN switches in solid-state transformers: Data Center Dynamics**
Enphase and Infineon have deployed 900-volt gallium nitride switches in solid-state transformers designed for AI data centers, and they call the deployment a world first. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/enphase-and-infineon-deploy-900v-gan-switches-in-solid-state-transformers-designed-for-ai-data-centers/)

**CoreWeave expands its global AI network to the Middle East and Asia Pacific: CoreWeave**
CoreWeave says its Global AI Network backbone runs at petabit scale, with MACsec encryption in hardware at line rate across the backbone and inside its data centers. New points of presence in the UAE, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Australia, South Korea and Japan are coming online beginning in the fourth quarter, taking the network to four continents. The company compares that capacity to streaming a 4K movie to 66 million people at once. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2115081179816698003)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**TSMC is reported preparing a CoWoS price rise of up to 20 percent: TIKR.com**
A day after the CoWoS backlog was already in view, Taiwan’s Commercial Times reports TSMC is preparing to raise CoWoS advanced-packaging prices by up to 20 percent, and TSMC has not confirmed it. The report, citing supply-chain sources, says foundries and outside packagers are preparing increases of 10 to 20 percent as demand has spread from AI GPUs to server CPUs and custom AI chips, with the bill landing on customers including NVIDIA and AMD. Equipment lead times are reported at six to eight months, from three to six. TIKR notes TSMC’s third-quarter revenue of $46.7 billion, a gross margin of 66.4 percent versus 59.5 percent a year earlier, advanced packaging at about 8 percent of 2025 revenue and expected slightly over 10 percent this year, and capex of $60 billion to $64 billion this year aimed mostly at capacity arriving in 2028 and 2029. Source: [tikr.com](https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmc-gains-3-on-reported-20-price-hike-for-ai-chip-packaging?)

**SEMI scales workforce programs as the U.S. talent gap nears 200,000: Semiconductor Digest**
Shari Liss, SEMI’s vice president of global workforce development, said the U.S. industry is going to be almost 200,000 people short in the next few years. Joe Stockunas, president of SEMI Americas, said talent is the top answer when members are asked what could hold back growth. The National Network for Microelectronics Education is a $200 million, five-year CHIPS-funded effort with the National Science Foundation and the Department of Commerce, operated by the SEMI Foundation. Its first four regional nodes bring together more than 325 partners. The foundation has an equipment-maintenance technician certification, and ChipPath lists about 199,000 job postings. SEMI is also standing up the India Semiconductor Academy, Taiwan training agreements for American students, a Global Schools Academy and a Chip the Future Challenge. Liss called federal funding a drop compared with what is needed. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/semi-scales-up-workforce-programs-as-u-s-talent-gap-nears-200000-2/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=semi-scales-up-workforce-programs-as-u-s-talent-gap-nears-200000-2)

**Solidigm drops a U.S. IPO review and is reported in $45 billion plant talks: EE Times**
SK Hynix has discontinued its review of a U.S. IPO for flash and SSD subsidiary Solidigm. CEO Kwak Noh Jung said the IPO was meant to raise outside capital for Solidigm production expansion, and that market conditions made proceeding now the wrong way to get that outcome. Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the negotiations, reports Solidigm is in talks with the U.S. Commerce Department about investing $45 billion in a new U.S. chip plant, which would be the first new major flash-memory production facility on American soil. Before committing, Solidigm is seeking U.S. government permission to send equipment to upgrade an existing plant in Dalian, China. Those are talks, not a committed fab. **Anduril teams with Qualcomm on a military laptop using TSMC Arizona: BigGo Finance**
Anduril is teaming with Qualcomm on a military-grade laptop whose core chips are to be made at TSMC’s Arizona fab. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/3439d8ba-2fe1-4117-b285-18bbf4d46e13)

**Anthropic's IPO filing says TSMC could not always supply enough chips: Forbes**
Anthropic’s IPO filing says TSMC could not always supply enough chips. Source: [forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/10/28/anthropics-ipo-filing-says-tsmc-couldnt-always-supply-enough-chips/)

**UC San Diego partners with TSMC on a classroom-to-cleanroom pipeline: UC San Diego Today**
UC San Diego is partnering with TSMC on a pipeline from the classroom into the semiconductor cleanroom. Source: [today.ucsd.edu](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/uc-san-diego-partners-with-tsmc-to-create-pipeline-from-the-classroom-to-semiconductor-cleanroom)

**Schneider Electric pilots a digital twin for Nscale AI infrastructure: HPCwire**
Schneider Electric, AVEVA, Nscale and Start Campus have piloted an immersive digital twin for Nscale’s AI infrastructure, built on the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and connecting Schneider, AVEVA and ETAP technology. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/schneider-electric-and-partners-pilot-digital-twin-for-nscales-ai-infrastructure/)

**TPG is reported eyeing UK data-center firm Ark: Data Center Dynamics**
TPG is reported to be eyeing UK data-center operator Ark at a possible $5 billion valuation, which is not a signed sale. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/tpg-eyes-uk-data-center-firm-ark-report/)

**AI chip packaging sizes approach four times the reticle limit: BigGo Finance**
BigGo Finance reports AI chip packaging sizes approaching four times the reticle limit, with the 2.5D roadmap contest described as running out to 2028. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/4eb5b699-fd87-4922-8d26-0463a5d2360e)

### The Teardown: A Molecule That Emits the Link
A spin that can be addressed one molecule at a time, and that emits a photon at a set optical frequency, is the part HPCwire’s account of NVision’s Nature paper treats as the missing connector. Until that interface existed, molecular spins could be interesting defects and still fail as qubits, because they could not be controlled individually and coherently. The paper, A Single-Molecule Spin-Photon Interface, is described as the first individually addressable organic molecular spin-photon interface. The molecule is a carbene. It is meant to be deposited as a thin film, the way OLED materials are deposited, straight onto a photonic integrated circuit, including HyperLight’s thin-film lithium niobate chiplets. Light, not a wire between neighboring dies, is the link that entangles a stationary spin with another spin on the same chip or on another chip.

That choice changes the floor plan. A monolithic quantum chip packs qubits until crosstalk, control wiring and heat set the spacing. NVision’s photonic integrated quantum circuit uses the optical link so the qubits do not have to sit in that tight neighborhood. The molecules run at 2 to 4 kelvin, not at the millikelvin stack many superconducting parts demand, and they emit at optical frequencies the photonic chip can take without a separate wavelength translation step. Chemistry is the design knob: memory time, gate speed and photon emission are tuned inside one molecule rather than by redrawing a silicon qubit cell. HPCwire reports the screen that produced the carbene: more than 150 candidate molecules evaluated, 40 of them synthesized in the lab.

The loss budget is the worked example, and it is why the foundry claim is not just a slogan. The platform is described as tolerating up to 70 percent photon loss and still operating on standard silicon photonics, instead of demanding an ultra-low-loss optical plant that most CMOS lines do not run. Take a link that throws away seven photons in every ten. If the interface still closes entanglement on the three that arrive, the interconnect can be a photonic chip a foundry already knows how to build, with HyperLight’s electro-optic lithium niobate sitting underneath a deposited molecular film. The alternative path in the same account is decades and multi-billion-dollar proprietary fabs for modalities that only scale inside a custom line. NVision’s commercial sketch puts the first integrated prototype chips in the fourth quarter of 2026, a live on-chip demonstration by the end of 2026, then a climb to 1,000 physical qubits and toward 1,000 logical, fault-tolerant qubits on chip by 2030, in a data-center form factor. Those dates are targets, not delivered systems.

The 70 percent figure is also the exit ramp. If a real photonic link loses more than that share of photons, standard silicon photonics stops being enough and the design is back in the specialized low-loss plant it was written to avoid. The same break appears if the thin-film deposit cannot keep the single-molecule addressability the Nature result showed in the lab, because a film that only works as an ensemble is not a qubit array a foundry can tile. And if the workload needs two-qubit gates that only exist when the spins share a neighborhood, the optical decoupling that removes crosstalk also removes the interaction, and proximity wins again. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/nvision-reports-molecular-qubit-advance-partners-with-hyperlight-on-photonic-chips/)

### On the Horizon
- CXMT’s reported HBM3E mass production is timed for the end of 2026, within about two months of this report.
- Intel’s 14A 1.0 process design kit is aimed at volume production early next year; the 0.9 kit for outside customers was targeted for October and is not described as handed over.
- CoreWeave’s new Middle East and Asia Pacific points of presence are scheduled to start coming online in the fourth quarter of 2026.
- NVision is targeting first prototype integrated chips in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a live on-chip demonstration by the end of 2026, with a 2030 goal of 1,000 logical qubits on chip.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **More than 400 gigawatts of planned data-center load is now chasing power.**

**What You Need to Know:** More than 400 gigawatts of new data-center load is in planning, and power — not the announcement — decides what gets built. Industrial Info Resources puts Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Google on pace to announce more than $700 billion of data-center spending this year, against a US fleet that is already 53 gigawatts. A reported CoWoS price rise and Anthropic’s IPO filing put packaging and Taiwan manufacturing on the same bill.

### Top Story
Industrial Info Resources, speaking at Data Center World Power in September and reported by Data Center Knowledge, expects Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Google to announce more than $700 billion of data-center spending this year, up from a combined $64 billion in 2018. The US now has 53 gigawatts of operational data-center load, up from 23 gigawatts in 2023, with another 42 gigawatts approved or under construction; IIR frames demand as moving from 35 gigawatts in 2024 to 125 gigawatts by 2030. More than 400 gigawatts of new data-center load is in planning, almost 100 US sites are designed for at least 1 gigawatt, and the US and Canada pipeline is about $4.75 trillion across more than 4,250 projects. IIR counts more than 500 data-center moratoria across 42 states and $130 billion of projects rejected in the first quarter of 2026; New York has a temporary ban on new data centers larger than 50 megawatts, and Texas has paused new grid interconnections while it works through about 200 gigawatts of requests. GE Vernova, Mitsubishi Power and Siemens Energy are sold out of larger gas turbines through 2029, with some orders stretching into 2031. Shane Mullins of IIR said that if a project needs more than 300 megawatts and the utility queue says 2034, building or contracting a gas plant is the fastest path; IIR also counts $228 billion of gas-plant projects across 347 grassroots, expansion and conversion jobs, 111 nuclear projects worth $311.4 billion including 61 small modular reactors, and 701 battery projects worth almost $200 billion. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/the-power-challenge-behind-hyperscale-ai-expansion)

### Silicon
**Micron Plans 400-Layer 3D NAND with Wafer-to-Wafer Bonding in 2027: TechPowerUp**
Micron has announced a plan, not a shipment, to bring G11 NAND to production and to ship 400-layer NAND in the second half of 2027. G9, which is shipping across the product line, uses more than 200 layers; G11 is meant to double module capacity by stacking a memory-cell wafer on a peripheral-logic wafer. The join is hybrid bonding, wafer to wafer, the structural approach YMTC has already used in Xtacking: metal bumps in the two wafers fuse into one chip. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354167/micron-plans-400-layer-3d-nand-with-wafer-to-wafer-bonding-in-2027)

**Intel to Acquire Classiq to Create a Full-stack Quantum Computing Platform: TechPowerUp**
Intel has entered a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, the company said on X and TechPowerUp reported from the announcement. The combination pairs Intel’s quantum software, silicon spin-qubit technology and manufacturing with Classiq’s automated quantum-algorithm synthesis platform, while Classiq’s software stays agnostic to qubit type and hardware. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said joining forces with Classiq turns Intel’s Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354153/intel-to-acquire-classiq-to-create-a-full-stack-quantum-computing-platform)

**Elon Musk Wanted 30,000 Of NVIDIA’s Bleeding Edge AI GPU Systems But Is Getting Just 20,000: Wccftech**
Wccftech reports analyst Jeff Pu’s claim that Elon Musk wanted 30,000 of NVIDIA’s latest AI GPU systems and is getting 20,000. Pu still calls that allocation enough to make Musk the biggest buyer in 2027. The figure is an analyst statement, not an NVIDIA shipment notice. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/elon-musk-wanted-30000-of-nvidias-bleeding-edge-ai-gpu-systems-but-is-getting-just-20000-still-enough-to-be-2027s-biggest-buyer-says-analyst-jeff-pu/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Developers Secure 10 TSMC Suppliers For $7B Halo Vista Mixed-Use Project: Bisnow**
Bisnow reports that developers have secured 10 TSMC suppliers for the $7 billion Halo Vista mixed-use project. That is a supplier commitment on a mixed-use development, not a reported energization. Source: [bisnow.com](https://www.bisnow.com/news/phoenix/industrial/developers-secure-10-tsmc-suppliers-for-7b-halo-vista-mixed-use-project)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Demand and Complexities of AI GPUs and Custom ASICs Have Stressed TSMC’s CoWoS Supply: Wccftech**
China Times supply-chain sources, reported by Wccftech and Yahoo Finance and not confirmed by TSMC, say the foundry is discussing a CoWoS price increase of 10 to 20 percent. The reported pressure is AI GPUs, custom ASICs and server CPUs that put more compute dies and HBM stacks on one package, which enlarges each unit, cuts hourly tool output and lengthens test. Wccftech says reported capacity is 130,000 monthly wafers in 2026 and 200,000 units in 2027; Yahoo, citing the same China Times report, says monthly capacity is expected to exceed 130,000 units in 2026 and 200,000 units next year, so the two accounts do not use the same unit word. Industry sources in the Wccftech account say a new advanced-packaging plant takes about three years to reach full load at its bottleneck stations, and equipment lead times have stretched from 3–6 months to 6–8 months. TSMC’s 5x-reticle CoWoS packages are in volume production, 9x and 14x versions are in development, and panel-based CoPoS is aimed at larger packages and lower cost; Yahoo names Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm and MediaTek among customers who would feel a higher packaging price. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/tsmc-cowos-price-hike-20-percent-ai-gpu-asic-demand/)

**Anthropic Warns Disruptions to TSMC’s Operations Could Hit AI Chip Supply: BusinessLine**
In a registration statement filed with the US SEC on October 26, Anthropic said most of the world’s most advanced chip manufacturing sits at TSMC in Taiwan, and that a disruption there would hit its ability to train and deploy models. The filing says military conflict, tariffs and trade restrictions, economic coercion, a blockade, a natural disaster, or a loss of electricity or water could severely disrupt advanced-chip supply, and that capacity outside Taiwan, including in the US, is still early-stage. It also says TSMC has at times been unable to meet full demand, leaving Anthropic short of chips on time. Seoul Economic Daily, reading the same filing, says Anthropic names SK hynix, Samsung Electronics and Micron as the main HBM producers and warns they may not deliver needed volumes on time, especially if other large buyers lock a supplier’s output. That paper’s simple sum of seven disclosed contracts is about $637 billion, led by a Broadcom AI-accelerator lease of about $161.2 billion, Google cloud commitments of at least $114.5 billion, Amazon of at least $110 billion and Microsoft of at least $44.9 billion, plus SpaceXAI, Nscale and Lambda; the paper says the total mixes minimums, equipment leases and volume-based amounts, so it is not one fixed investment. Anthropic’s computing and infrastructure costs were $8.945 billion in the first half of this year, up 283 percent, while revenue rose to $16.286 billion from $1.163 billion. Source: [thehindubusinessline.com](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/anthropic-warns-disruptions-to-tsmcs-operations-could-hit-ai-chip-supply-threaten-business/article71629778.ece)

### Also Today
**Intel "Raptor Lake Next" 16-Core and 20-Core CPUs Surface: TechPowerUp**
Shipping manifests and an internal driver, reported by Tom’s Hardware and TechPowerUp, show unannounced LGA-1700 “Raptor Lake Next” parts, including a 16-core, 125-watt SKU at 3.5 gigahertz with 30 megabytes of cache and a 20-core, 65-watt SKU at 2.1 gigahertz with 33 megabytes. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354145/intel-raptor-lake-next-16-core-and-20-core-cpus-surface)

**Northern Arizona University and TSMC Offer Career Training Without a Degree: Signals AZ**
Northern Arizona University and TSMC are offering career training that does not require a degree. Source: [signalsaz.com](https://www.signalsaz.com/articles/northern-arizona-university-and-tsmc-offer-career-training-without-a-degree/)

### The Teardown: When the Advance Payment Buys the Slot
Wafer, high-bandwidth memory, a packaging substrate and a test socket can each stop an AI chip, so the delivery date is no longer set by the foundry handoff alone. 36Kr describes the older chain as a defined split: design houses specified the part, wafer foundries manufactured it, and packaging and test plants took the next step, joined by orders and shared standards. That split assumed each link could be booked after the one before it. AI parts broke the sequence because the performance ceiling is set together by the advanced process, the memory and the package. A larger die and a larger package also consume more wafer and more packaging area per chip, so a shortage in one input idles the others.

The wafer side is already spoken for. TrendForce estimated in March 2026 that global foundry revenue would rise 24.8 percent for the full year, to about $218.8 billion, and that TSMC’s 5-nanometer, 4-nanometer and more advanced capacity would stay fully loaded through the end of 2026. 36Kr says that load is Nvidia and AMD GPUs plus custom chips from Google, AWS and Meta. A full advanced-node line does not finish the accelerator if the package, the substrate or the test insertion is late. The scarce object stops being a wafer start and becomes a reserved place in every downstream tool.

The reservation is now paid before the tools exist. In July 2026 Amkor signed a $1.5 billion multi-year advanced-packaging and development agreement with Nvidia, and Nvidia’s advance payment was to support Amkor’s US capacity build. On October 21 the two added a South Korea expansion; 36Kr puts the US and Korea agreements together at $3 billion. Test follows the same pattern. Nvidia provided $1.1 billion to King Yuan Electronics as a capacity-reservation advance, funding a US test factory and the equipment to run it. On substrates, the October 21 arrangements with Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and XinXing Electronics are planned to take the relevant substrate capacity to 2.5 times the current level, and Ibiden’s expansion of its Ono plant in Japan is also backed by an Nvidia advance. Cash plus a multi-year volume promise moves a supplier’s build plan earlier than a spot order would. The supplier gets a demand signal it can borrow against; the customer gets a claim on capacity that a later purchase order might not secure.

That choice stops being the right way to buy a chip when the check lands on a link that is not the late one. 36Kr notes that 2.5D packaging of the CoWoS type has been tight since 2023 and that the squeeze has spread to packaging equipment, substrates and key materials, so more wafers, or even a larger packaging house, still leave delivery gated by whichever input did not get the money. It also stops working for anyone but the largest buyers once the line is allocated by who can write the advance. 36Kr’s warning is polarization: firms with capital and the ability to commit long orders take scarce capacity first. A reservation that clears the bottleneck only for those buyers fails the moment the missing part is a tool, a substrate or a material the prepaid supplier cannot pull forward, and it fails the buyer who needs the chip but cannot fund the factory that has to build it. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4043465786889350)

### On the Horizon
- April 2027: King Yuan’s US test factory, funded by Nvidia’s $1.1 billion capacity-reservation advance, has a mass-production target of April 2027, 36Kr reported.
- Three years from the October 21, 2026 substrate agreements: Nvidia’s plan with Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and XinXing Electronics is to lift relevant substrate capacity to 2.5 times the current level inside that window.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **3.6 gigawatts of contracted power now back SWI Compute's planned NVIDIA factories in Europe.**

**What You Need to Know:** SWI Compute emerged from stealth with 3.6 gigawatts of secured power and about $1 billion of NVIDIA systems on order, starting with an announced 30-megawatt factory in the UK. NVIDIA's updated Vera Rubin NVL72 sheet cuts rack memory bandwidth to 1,400 TB/s. E2E Networks has proposed 5.4 MW more for HGX B300 and other Blackwell GPUs on top of about 9.2 MW already in service.

### Top Story
SWI Compute's first large-scale AI factory is announced at 30 MW in the UK, with close to 7,000 Rubin GPUs and 3,500 Vera CPUs in NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks expected online by the end of 2027. That 30 MW is the initial phase of a UK campus planned to grow to 530 MW, and the company's first step toward 2.3 GW of NVIDIA AI factory capacity by 2029. SWI Group says it holds 3.6 GW of power capacity across 24 sites in Europe and the US after six years securing land, power and shell; five campuses sit in Ireland, the UK, Denmark, Spain and Italy, and one is already leased to a major hyperscaler. The new company became a Preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner in August, has ordered approximately $1 billion of NVIDIA systems, and says it has finalized contracts with its first customers, including a US-based AI inference platform. The first deployment is specified as NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra, with Vera CPU racks to follow, linked by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet; Delta Computers is the systems integrator for a build the company describes as more than 8,000 GPUs. From 2027, new sites, starting with the UK campus, are to follow the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX reference design, which NVIDIA says can put up to 40% more GPU capacity in the same power budget. Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/prnewswire:01e3224148259:0-swi-compute-emerges-from-stealth-to-turn-gigawatts-of-power-into-nvidia-ai-factories-starting-in-europe/)

### Silicon
**NVIDIA Cuts HBM4 Speed and NVLink Bandwidth Targets for Vera Rubin: TechPowerUp**
Yesterday the open question on the roadmap was whether announced rack targets would still be the ones that ship; TechPowerUp now reports that NVIDIA has cut them on the updated Vera Rubin specification sheet. HBM4 speed on that sheet moves from 11.7 Gbps per pin to 9.6 Gbps per pin, and Vera Rubin NVL72 total memory bandwidth moves from the previously advertised 1,580 TB/s to 1,400 TB/s. NVLink bandwidth per GPU falls from 1.8 TB/s to 1.5 TB/s, and bidirectional NVLink GPU bandwidth from 3.6 TB/s to 3 TB/s. TechPowerUp reports the NVLink Nyquist frequency target was lowered from 56 GHz to 47 GHz so the SerDes, cables and materials face an easier electrical demand, accepting less peak bandwidth for yield and stability. The outlet says the memory-speed cut is not laid directly on NVIDIA's suppliers, and reads it as NVIDIA's bus width and signaling not supporting the higher rate. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354133/nvidia-cuts-hbm4-speed-and-nvlink-bandwidth-targets-for-vera-rubin)

**Silicon Photonic Modulator Reaches 200 Gb/s PAM4 With Reduced DSP: Semiconductor Engineering**
Researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo, Yokohama National University, AIST and the Photonics Electronics Technology Research Association reported a low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator aimed at multi-terabit optical interconnects for AI data centers. The device is described as 200G per wavelength PAM4 with reduced DSP, using a built-in electro-optic equalizer. The paper sets that approach against conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators, which the authors say struggle to meet the speed, energy and size those links need. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/silicon-photonic-modulator-reaches-200-gb-s-pam4-with-reduced-dsp-science-tokyo-yokohama-aist-petra/)

**Vertical DRAM Stacking Expands Thermal Design Space Beyond HBM-on-GPU: Semiconductor Engineering**
imec researchers evaluated a 3D memory stack that rotates DRAM dies vertically above a GPU and puts cooling cavities between the dies, as an alternative to conventional 2.5D HBM and to HBM stacked directly on the GPU. Package-level thermal simulations in the September 2026 paper vary stack height, memory capacity and organization, cooling-cavity materials, stack orientation, mold insertion, and a distributed memory-controller and network-on-chip tier. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/vertical-dram-stacking-expands-thermal-design-space-beyond-hbm-imec/)

### Data Centres & Power
**E2E Networks proposes 5.4 MW for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs: Dalal Street Investment Journal**
E2E Networks has proposed about 5.4 MW of additional capacity for NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell GPUs, on top of existing capacity of around 9.2 MW, which would take the total to roughly 14.6 MW, nearly 59% above the current base. The company says the addition follows its infrastructure plan and expected AI-compute demand, and that it will fund the work from internal accruals and debt rather than an equity raise. In FY2025-26, revenue from operations rose 49.78% to Rs 245.58 crore, operating cash flow rose to Rs 122.06 crore, and higher depreciation on new infrastructure produced a net loss of Rs 15.57 crore. September 2026 quarter net sales were Rs 223.76 crore, with a profit-before-interest-depreciation-and-tax margin, excluding other income, of 76.63%; management has tied recent operating momentum to Blackwell deployments. A flagship Blackwell deployment linked to a contract of nearly Rs 1,000 crore through June 2029 is fully utilised. Larsen & Toubro held 16.57% as of the September 2026 quarter, and foreign institutional investors moved from 1.27% to 2.53% in that period. Source: [insights.dsij.in](https://insights.dsij.in/dsijarticledetail/ai-stock-hits-upper-circuit-after-announcing-nvidia-gpu-expansion-plans-fiis-nearly-double-their-stake) · [scanx.trade](https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/e2e-networks-plans-5-4-mw-capacity-expansion-ai-services/54550643)

**117.5 GW of behind-the-meter power orders: Dylan Patel**
Dylan Patel wrote that there are 117.5 GW of behind-the-meter power orders being delivered and installed over the next few years. In a follow-up he separated that kind of order book from capacity being energized, and said orders are much larger than the energized figure he was correcting. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2114292929691046271) · [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2114398591112647089)

**Ukrainian drone attacks hammer Russia's finance ministry data center: Tom's Hardware**
After earlier strikes on Russian data-center sites, Tom's Hardware reports drone attacks damaged a finance ministry facility that reports describe as one of three the ministry operated. The damaged site reportedly holds tax databases and other state-registry data. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/ukrainian-drone-attacks-hammer-russias-finance-ministry-data-center-damaged-facility-reportedly-holds-tax-databases-facility-also-holds-other-important-state-registry-data)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Bringing Down Test Costs For Co-Packaged Optics: Semiconductor Engineering**
A Semiconductor Engineering panel — Matt Griffin of Teradyne, Ira Leventhal of Advantest, Dave Armstrong of ISE Labs, and Kazuo Yamaguchi of Keysight — says optical-component test cost is high and approaching manufacturing cost. Leventhal's frame for the budget is that an inexpensive optical engine cannot be allowed to take down a $40,000 or $50,000 GPU or ASIC. Customers are adding monitor photodiodes and loopback taps so a failed bit-error result can be traced, while a "golden" laser is treated by test engineers as a known-good source rather than the device under test. A retimed near-packaged engine can be compliance-tested on its own DSP; a linear-drive engine, and co-packaged optics, share one electrical-optical path, so a failed link is harder to pin on either side, and rework after attach remains a reason to demand known-good optical engines even when they can be detached. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/bringing-down-test-costs-for-co-packaged-optics/)

**Data-center buyers and a Samsung HBM premium: Wccftech**
Wccftech reports that data-center customers are paying more for what it calls a superior HBM supply chain, and that Samsung is estimated to charge up to 25% extra. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/samsung-hbm-pricing-premium-data-center-supply-chain/)

**NVIDIA software at about $2,000 per GPU per year: TechPowerUp**
At a GTC Berlin Q&A, Jensen Huang said software licensing will be a growing part of NVIDIA's business and that it costs about $2,000 per GPU per year to run the NVIDIA software that powers agents in AI factories, a figure TechPowerUp, following The Register, treats as an example rather than a formal price. NVIDIA's own licensing guide lists AI Enterprise at $4,500 per GPU for one year with support, or $18,000 per GPU for five years. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354113/nvidia-eyes-software-revenue-with-a-usd-2-000-per-gpu-yearly-figure-from-huang)

### The Teardown: Useful Life in Vacuum
In vacuum, convective cooling does not exist. Heat leaving a processor has to be conducted or pumped to an outer surface, and that surface has to radiate the energy away. EE Times, writing on Google's Project Suncatcher, treats the radiator, the solar arrays, the power distribution and the years the hardware must survive as part of the processor's real performance, because a failed board in orbit is not swapped at the next maintenance window.

On October 1, 2026, a Project Suncatcher prototype reached orbit aboard a SpaceX mission. Developed with Planet, the satellite established contact with the ground. Its task is to test how commercial AI hardware behaves where replacement is not available. Before launch, Google subjected Trillium TPUs to vibration and proton-beam tests and reported encouraging tolerance to accumulated ionizing radiation, while still investigating errors that arise during AI workloads. It also tested a thermal system of heat pipes and radiators in simulated vacuum. Laboratory exposure is an initial indication of resilience. The flight still has to establish the rate of faults, and what those faults do to sustained output, over years.

The plant required to turn that experiment into something like a data center shows up in a model, not in the satellite now on orbit. An April 2026 study by Slava Turyshev, as EE Times recounts it, examined a representative one-megawatt installation and required approximately 5,640 square meters of photovoltaic arrays and 2,500 square meters of radiators. Those are model outputs, dependent on assumptions about solar generation and heat rejection. They are the physical scale of one megawatt, still small beside a terrestrial hyperscale hall, and every square meter is mass that has to be launched. A spacecraft also needs electrical generation and distribution, provision for periods of insufficient sunlight, and data links both between satellites and back to Earth. Each kilogram lands in the launch budget.

The processor sets part of that mass. A faster accelerator that draws more power can require larger solar arrays, more electrical distribution equipment and more radiating surface. Those supporting pieces add mass and can offset the benefit of higher throughput. Software efficiency, error rates, utilization and expected service life all move the comparison between two chips with similar benchmark scores. Take two architectures on the same workload. One completes more operations per second and needs a larger thermal system. The other is slower, draws less power, and allows a smaller spacecraft that may fly a longer mission. The useful comparison is total computation completed over the mission, adjusted for interruptions, degraded operation and the chance of premature failure. A processor that wins the initial benchmark can still deliver fewer productive hours before the spacecraft is retired. For an operator that cannot replace a failed board, that lost lifetime output is a direct cost.

Turyshev's model also examines launch cost, spacecraft construction, utilization and operating life. Under one set of assumptions, the combined cost of launch and spacecraft construction would have to fall below a benchmark based on the published price of a dedicated Falcon 9 launch for the modeled system to compete. That comparison is sensitive to the launch configuration chosen, and it says little about future launch prices. The U.S. Government Accountability Office, in an April assessment, identified cooling, communications and deployment economics as unresolved. Processing observations near the satellites that collect them is the earlier use case, because less raw data might need to be sent to Earth. A general-purpose orbital data center faces the larger infrastructure problem. Communications sit beside power and heat: a distributed workload that moves data often between processors makes the network part of the system cost, and a functioning accelerator does not by itself make the power, thermal and link systems work together at commercial scale.

NASA's High-Performance Spaceflight Computing processor, developed with Microchip Technology, is specified for spacecraft workloads that need autonomy, radiation resilience, power management and fault tolerance. In May 2026, NASA reported preliminary testing that suggested performance roughly 500 times that of radiation-hardened processors then in use. The same lifetime arithmetic applies: throughput only counts for the hours the machine keeps producing.

This design choice stops being the right one when the extra array and radiator a hotter accelerator demands consume the mission mass budget before those extra operations are delivered, or when the job is only local reduction of sensor data and never required a megawatt of general-purpose compute in orbit. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/in-orbit-useful-life-becomes-a-performance-metric/)

### On the Horizon
- In 2027, Google's planned two-satellite optical-link experiment is meant to test high-bandwidth connections between spacecraft.
- Starting in the fourth quarter of 2027, SWI Compute's next generation of AI campuses across Europe is scheduled to come online.
- Samsung has said it will be in production with High-NA EUV by 2028; TSMC has said it intends to use High-NA in high-volume manufacturing for advanced nodes starting in 2030.
- TSMC and ASML have targeted a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031.
