# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Fifty gigawatts in 2027 would equal every data centre built through 2024.**

**What You Need to Know:** SemiAnalysis argues that about fifty gigawatts of data-centre capacity in 2027 would match the entire global data-centre market built through 2024, and it points to more than twenty-four gigawatts already in advanced construction for that year. A separate supply read puts next year’s high-bandwidth memory demand near 61.5 billion gigabits against expected shipments near 54.6 billion gigabits. Packaging is the other capacity bet: a U.S. interposer line for TSMC, and higher back-end spending at ASE, Amkor and Micron.

### Top Story
Datacenters 2027: The Year of Acceleration, +50GW in a Single Year: SemiAnalysis
SemiAnalysis says one photograph set covers more than 24 gigawatts of data centres in an advanced stage of construction, across 40 campuses, most of them more than halfway done with exterior cooling and electrical equipment already installed, and all of them to be delivered in 2027. Those 40 campuses are described as a small share of the several hundred sites the firm tracks in an advanced stage of construction. Year to date, slightly under 1 trillion dollars of binding, non-cancellable data-centre leases have been signed. A typical contract runs 15 to 20 years, with a total contract value of 30 to 50 billion dollars per gigawatt, and developers typically spend only 5 to 10 percent of project capital without a customer. The same piece also refers to a plus-43-gigawatt 2027 forecast that Altimeter’s Brad Gerstner called too aggressive against his own figure of about 25 gigawatts. Source: [newsletter.semianalysis.com](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/datacenters-2027-the-year-of-acceleration)

### Silicon
Breaking The Memory Bottleneck In AI And HPC SoCs: Semiconductor Engineering
Semiconductor Engineering’s write-up of a Synopsys paper says embedded memory, not compute, now consumes more than half of total die area on AI and HPC system-on-chips and constrains bandwidth, latency and energy. Silicon results from SRAM and register-file test chips on Intel’s 18A process, using RibbonFET and PowerVia, show density improvements in the 5 to 10 percent range and iso-power performance gains of up to about 4 percent. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/breaking-the-memory-bottleneck-in-ai-and-hpc-socs/)

### Data Centres & Power
Why Data Centers Rarely Reuse Cooling Water: Data Center Knowledge
Data Center Knowledge says a 100-megawatt facility can consume about 2.5 billion litres of water a year, roughly as much as 5,000 or more homes, mostly to reject heat. The most common method is direct evaporative cooling, drawing air through wetted media so evaporation removes heat from the airstream. Most sites do not recycle that water, the piece says, because alternatives carry higher capital cost and more operational complexity than the economics currently justify. Uptime Institute adds that water use has no standard template: each location has its own water signature, legacy halls often rely on open evaporative cooling towers, and new halls can be built to use little or no water for cooling. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/cooling/why-data-centers-rarely-reuse-cooling-water)

### Supply Chain & Policy
Samsung Works with TSMC on Nvidia’s Custom HBM: SammyGuru
SammyGuru, citing industry estimates, says high-bandwidth memory demand next year is about 61.5 billion gigabits, up 91 percent from this year, while memory makers may ship only 54.6 billion gigabits, a gap of about 10 percent. The same account says Nvidia’s custom stack, NVHBM, uses a physical layer 60 percent smaller than standard HBM, and that TSMC’s 3-nanometer yield is estimated above 90 percent against about 60 percent for Samsung’s comparable 2-nanometer SF2 process. Samsung’s own 4-nanometer base-die output is limited to Hwaseong Line 17 and part of Pyeongtaek P3. Benzinga, citing Seoul Economic Daily, adds that NVHBM can deliver up to 30 percent more memory bandwidth and 15 percent lower power than standard HBM4E, that Nvidia wants the core die standardized on sixth-generation 1c DRAM, and that Samsung’s Device Solutions division accepted the 3-nanometer base-die request after an internal review. TSMC declined to comment on individual customers. Source: [sammyguru.com](https://sammyguru.com/samsung-works-with-tsmc-on-nvidia-custom-hbm/)

GlobalFoundries to build TSMC silicon interposers in Malta: Silicon UK
GlobalFoundries will manufacture the silicon interposer for TSMC’s CoWoS packaging under a deal valued at 2 billion dollars over five years, expanding capacity at its plant in Malta, New York, so TSMC customers can market products as manufactured and packaged entirely in the United States. Ed Kaste, senior vice president of CMOS at GlobalFoundries, said the deal would create a secure source of advanced-packaging elements. Silicon UK also reports that TSMC last week said it would invest 100 billion dollars to expand existing Phoenix operations, on top of 165 billion dollars already committed, and that many advanced chips built in Arizona are still sent back to Taiwan for final assembly. TSMC began 4-nanometer production in Arizona in January of last year. Source: [silicon.co.uk](https://www.silicon.co.uk/workspace/components/globalfoundries-tsmc-631852)

Advanced packaging capex rises as the EUV lesson moves to the back end: BigGo Finance
BigGo Finance reports TSMC is keeping this year’s capital-expenditure forecast at 60 to 64 billion dollars, with 10 to 20 percent of that going to advanced packaging, testing and photomask production, and CoWoS capacity the focus. ASE Technology raised this year’s capital-expenditure plan from 8.5 billion dollars to 10.5 billion dollars. Amkor’s second-phase expansion of its Arizona campus lifts total investment to about 12 billion dollars. Micron is investing about 7 billion dollars in Singapore for an HBM packaging hub. Yole Group projects the advanced-packaging market from 55 billion dollars in 2025 to more than 120 billion dollars by 2031, and more than half of total semiconductor packaging revenue by 2031. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/f6021721-ea46-4577-847e-68fe4d33346e)

### The Teardown: When the Pad Has to Land Inside Forty Nanometres
Hybrid bonding mates a dielectric face and a metal pad in the same step, so the interconnect can sit on a pitch a solder bump or a thermocompression bond has trouble holding. The copper has to land on copper. Alignment is the bond, not a check that happens after the chemistry.

The surface has to arrive flat, clean, and in a known material state. BigGo Finance quotes Applied Materials executive Prabu Raja: “Advanced packaging is no longer just physical assembly in the back end—it is a materials engineering revolution that demands wafer-level precision and cleanliness.” A particle, a recessed copper pad, or an unstable surface from an earlier step can make the bonder’s own positioning accuracy meaningless. That is the reason Applied Materials and Besi, starting from a joint R&D project in Singapore in 2020, built the Kinex die-to-wafer system to pull surface treatment, cleaning, activation and alignment into one tighter flow.

The measured case in that account is a May result from Imec and EV Group. They reached a 200-nanometre copper interconnect pitch in wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonding research. After bonding, overlay deviation of the copper pads stayed below 40 nanometres across all test chips on 300-millimetre wafers. Forty nanometres is one fifth of a 200-nanometre pitch. If the pad is on the order of that pitch, a 40-nanometre miss already consumes a large share of the contact before corrosion or dishing is counted. Imec, in the same report, says further scaling still has to solve surface topography from chemical mechanical polishing, copper corrosion, dielectric reliability, and metal diffusion along the bond interface.

The lithography tool beside that problem is already shipping, and it is not a bonder. ASML delivered the TWINSCAN XT:260 i-line system for 3D integration and advanced packaging in 2025, specified at 270 wafers an hour. Scanning 270 wafers an hour prints packaging layers. It does not join the pads. An international patent published on 15 May, with ASML Netherlands as applicant, discusses improving bonding-alignment deviation by controlling the surface state of the substrate support. BigGo Finance draws the line in plain terms: ASML has not publicly confirmed a commercial delivery timeline, customer qualification, or mass-production performance for hybrid-bonding equipment. A patent position is not a qualified tool on a high-bandwidth-memory line.

The R&D money shows how early the integrated flow still is. On 1 October, Besi became an innovation partner at Applied Materials’ EPIC centre in Silicon Valley, planned at up to about 5 billion dollars and spent as customer projects advance. The scope moves past die-to-wafer hybrid bonding into thermocompression-bond scaling, die-to-die, die-to-panel, and optical interconnects. Five days later, Applied Materials deepened work with Intel that includes Foveros 3D packaging. Lam Research’s path stays on the hole and the fill: Syndion deep reactive-ion etch for high-aspect-ratio through-silicon vias, and the SABRE 3D copper-plating platform for via fill, wafer-level packaging and redistribution layers. That coverage does not replace the bonder.

Hybrid bonding stops being the right next step on an HBM flow when the added surface-control steps raise the cost of the whole stack faster than the pitch gain pays back, or when polishing topography, copper corrosion, dielectric reliability or interface diffusion cannot be held inside the overlay the pitch requires. BigGo Finance says Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron still have to decide which HBM generation and which stack architecture split traditional thermocompression bonding from hybrid bonding. Until that yield, capacity and reliability sum closes, the 200-nanometre pitch remains a research result on 300-millimetre wafers, not a committed process split. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/1e451252-79da-45e8-9f64-39e900da59c1)

### On the Horizon
- GlobalFoundries aims to begin volume production of silicon interposers at Malta, New York, in the first half of 2028.
- TSMC’s packaging plant in Arizona is expected to begin operations in 2029.
- SK Hynix is targeting mass production by late 2029 at HBM advanced-packaging lines in Cheongju and in West Lafayette, Indiana.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Only 2.3 gigawatts looks delayed despite more than 300 local data-center bans.**

**What You Need to Know:** SemiAnalysis finds that more than 300 local data-center moratoriums are likely to delay only about 2.3 gigawatts, inside roughly 21 gigawatts sitting in moratorium areas. The same audit still has 38 gigawatts of U.S. data-center IT capacity coming online in 2027. Separately, Samsung is set to build Nvidia’s custom high-bandwidth-memory base dies on TSMC’s three-nanometre process.

### Top Story
Tom's Hardware reports a SemiAnalysis audit that finds more than 300 local data-center moratoriums likely to delay only three projects. Those three account for about 2.3 gigawatts of roughly 21 gigawatts located in moratorium areas, and that delay total leaves out Texas’s TCEQ permit pause. The firm’s forecast of 38 gigawatts of U.S. data-center IT capacity in 2027, more than double 2026, has barely moved over the last 12 months. Of that 2027 total, 22 gigawatts is under vertical construction and 16 gigawatts is mostly financed, with site work underway. Enacted local moratoriums cover about 20 gigawatts, of which about 1.5 gigawatts is delayed, and New York’s pause adds 0.8 gigawatts. A moratorium here is a temporary legal pause, almost always a freeze on new applications, and it moves a delivery date only if it reaches the parcel, stays in force, overlaps the schedule, and covers a use the project cannot work around. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/300-plus-local-data-center-bans-have-only-delayed-just-three-us-projects-bans-much-more-bark-than-bite-only-2-3-gigawatts-of-data-centers-are-held-up-versus-38-gigawatts-expected-online-in-2027)

### Silicon
**Samsung to use TSMC’s 3nm process for Nvidia NVHBM base dies: The Edge Malaysia**
Samsung will use TSMC’s three-nanometre process for base dies on Nvidia’s custom high-bandwidth memory, NVHBM, the first time Samsung has worked with TSMC at the HBM manufacturing stage, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use that process for the base dies and sixth-generation 1c DRAM for the core dies. NVHBM, unveiled in August and built on HBM4E, puts Nvidia’s memory controller on the base die. BigGo Finance reports the physical-layer area cut by 60 percent versus standard HBM, for up to 30 percent more bandwidth and 15 percent lower power than standard HBM4E. Industry estimates put TSMC’s 3nm yield above 90 percent and Samsung Foundry’s 2nm SF2 process near 60 percent. Samsung keeps its own 4nm turnkey base dies for standard HBM4 and HBM4E and for custom parts for other customers, including AMD, and is validating an NVHBM base die on its 2nm process if TSMC capacity fills up. Source: [theedgemalaysia.com](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/822222) · [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/samsung-use-tsmc-technology-nvidias-next-generation-memory-chips-seoul-newspaper-2026-10-18/) · [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/e7075834-0499-4217-ab8e-9bd80c85dc1e)

**Intel Razor Lake-AX quoted at 700 TOPS: TechPowerUp**
Intel senior vice president Cho Min-sung said at the Semiconductors Powering Humanoids summit in South Korea that Razor Lake-AX will carry 700 TOPS of on-die AI compute at INT8/FP8. TechPowerUp puts that at 3.88 times the 180 TOPS it attributes to current Panther Lake mobile chips. Earlier reports cited by the outlet describe a 16-core integrated GPU and a 32-core flagship integrated GPU on Xe3, and a GPU die of about 162.84 square millimetres. The same reports say on-package LPDDR5X or LPDDR6 returns with this AX part, and the image with the story is an illustration, not the package. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353825/intel-razor-lake-ax-to-pack-700-tops-of-ai-compute)

### Data Centres & Power
**Local pauses miss the parcel, the permit, or the clock: Tom's Hardware**
SemiAnalysis is tracking more than 400 local instruments across 17 states as of September, including a few permanent zoning bans, and New York, Texas, Pennsylvania and Oregon each acted in under two months this summer. Michigan has 45 enacted moratoriums and effectively zero pipeline exposure, with a Google campus on industrial land already zoned for data processing. SpaceX’s planned data center in Brownsville, Texas, sits on land the city removed from its limits, so the city moratorium does not reach it. In Pennsylvania a township pause landed before NorthPoint filed its special exception, pushing local approval to next year, and the company is still pursuing the project. The Economist’s Archie Hall, cited from a Michigan and Ohio trip, calls the moratoriums much more bark than bite for now. An August poll by the firm found more Americans negative than positive on data centers, and the analysis says pauses would need to be materially more widespread and restrictive to delay the buildout. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/300-plus-local-data-center-bans-have-only-delayed-just-three-us-projects-bans-much-more-bark-than-bite-only-2-3-gigawatts-of-data-centers-are-held-up-versus-38-gigawatts-expected-online-in-2027)

**Texas tells its environmental regulator to stop data-center permits: Tom's Hardware**
Texas Governor Greg Abbott told the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to issue no permits for data-center projects. Law firm Bracewell says that instruction applies whether or not a project is in ERCOT’s queue. SemiAnalysis analyst Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros said on the firm’s podcast last month that a strict state-level moratorium blocking even off-grid projects is the case that would worry the forecast, and he cited Texas. New York Governor Kathy Hochul, like Abbott, bypassed the legislature for a pause the governor controls and can revoke. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/300-plus-local-data-center-bans-have-only-delayed-just-three-us-projects-bans-much-more-bark-than-bite-only-2-3-gigawatts-of-data-centers-are-held-up-versus-38-gigawatts-expected-online-in-2027)

**Saras samples a 2 mm capacitor for vertical power delivery: Semiconductor Digest**
Semiconductor Digest reports that Saras Micro Devices is sampling a new 2 mm capacitor meant to be built into the PCB or the package core. The part is aimed at the vertical power delivery AI accelerators need. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/saras-micro-devices-embeds-capacitors-to-power-ai-accelerators/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=saras-micro-devices-embeds-capacitors-to-power-ai-accelerators)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**UBS puts next year’s HBM bits 11 percent short: BigGo Finance**
UBS, cited by BigGo Finance, projects next year’s HBM demand at about 61.5 billion gigabits, up 91 percent, against new shipments of 54.6 billion gigabits, up 49 percent, an 11 percent shortfall. Samsung’s 1c core dies run at Hwaseong Line 17 and Pyeongtaek P2, P3 and P4. The P5-1 facility, under construction, is slated to center on 1c lines. Samsung’s 4nm base-die lines are limited to portions of Hwaseong Line 17 and Pyeongtaek P3. TSMC, at its 15 October earnings announcement, said it will add two 3nm lines at Fab 18 in Tainan and also plans 3nm lines at its second Arizona fab and its second Kumamoto fab. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/e7075834-0499-4217-ab8e-9bd80c85dc1e)

**A 1.4 nm wafer is put near $45,000 as A14 pulls forward: The News International**
A J.P. Morgan note reported by The News International says TSMC is likely to bring its 1.4-nanometre node, A14, into mass production in the first half of 2028, earlier than prior reports of the second half of that year. Each 1.4 nm wafer is estimated at $45,000, about half again a 2 nm wafer Digitimes put near $30,000. The company intends to spread A14 across four facilities at its Central Taiwan site. Apple is reportedly planning 1.4 nm for the A22 Pro in high-end iPhones in 2028, and TrendForce is cited for Intel being considered a secondary provider. Qualcomm and MediaTek are expected to stay on 2 nm for one more generation because handset demand is already weak from the DRAM shortage. Source: [thenews.com.pk](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1420399-tsmc-apple-eye-14nm-chips-as-costs-surge-ahead-of-2028)

**A leaker puts PlayStation 6 memory and flash above $680: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp reports that hardware leaker KeplerL2 claims PlayStation 6 RAM and NAND flash alone cost over $680. The same leaker put the console bill of materials near $760 in March and roughly $960 in July. Leaks cited in the piece describe GDDR7 on a 160-bit bus, support for up to 40 GB, with 30 GB treated as more likely. The report says Sony looked at cutting memory capacity because AI data centers are absorbing DRAM and NAND supply. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353834/ps6-ram-and-storage-alone-reportedly-cost-sony-over-usd-680-claims-leaker)

### The Teardown: When One Pool Has to Hold the Scene
A core that cannot see its weights in the same address space has to wait for a copy. iTWire’s account of Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops describes the machine that tries to delete that wait: one superchip, a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores beside a Grace CPU with up to 20 cores, joined by NVLink-C2C, sharing up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory and rated at up to 1 petaflop of FP4. MediaTek’s piece of that CPU, the same report says, was power efficiency and connectivity. The mechanism is the pool, not the logo on the lid. On a split PC the GPU owns a private frame buffer. A tensor that begins in system memory is copied across a peripheral link, used, and often copied back before the CPU can trust it. Unified memory makes the CPU and the GPU clients of one physical pool. A load from either side is an address in that pool. Coherence is the interconnect’s job. If the line is already there, nobody stages a second copy to make the other processor legal. FP4 is the precision tied to the 1-petaflop rating. Four-bit weights are how 128 gigabytes holds a larger network than a wider format would allow in the same bytes. That rating is a peak at FP4. It is not a second number for FP8 or FP16, where the same cores move less work per watt and the same pool holds fewer parameters.

Walk only the figures iTWire prints. Systems from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI start at $2,399, the figure in Nvidia's announcement; iTWire's report put it at $2,399. Set the memory ceiling at 128 gigabytes and set Nvidia’s reported scene claim beside it: 3D scenes of up to 90 gigabytes. That scene is not a side buffer. It is most of the only pool the chip has. The operating system, the tool, and any agent mapped into the same addresses have to live in what the scene does not already occupy. There is no second tier in the description to spill into. An edit and a local model, if both are open, are roommates in that 128 gigabytes, which is the product claim of one PC for creation, gaming and personal agents. The gaming line next to it is AAA titles at 1440p at over 100 frames per second, a shader-and-bandwidth claim on those 6,144 CUDA cores, not evidence of a private graphics memory beside the pool. Adobe is optimising Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D for the platform, with up to 2x gains in beta builds at launch. A gain of that size on tools that stream large frames is what shows up when a peripheral copy was a large share of the old timeline. The Grace side, up to 20 cores, is the control plane: scheduling, I/O, the agent loop. It is not a second accelerator hiding in the same package. At a $2,399 start the comparison is not a data-centre GPU tray. It is whether one coherent pool, capped at these figures, replaces a desktop that split CPU DRAM from GPU memory and paid the copy on every handoff.

The single superchip stops being the right box when the live working set no longer fits in 128 gigabytes, or when the result required is not an FP4 peak of 1 petaflop. A 90-gigabyte scene already takes most of the pool. A second scene, a weight that will not quantise to four bits, or a context that has to stay wide, turns the next address into a miss this package cannot cure by adding a card. The partner list and the $2,399 floor do not move that ceiling. The ceiling is the pool. Source: [itwire.com](https://itwire.com/business-it-news/hardware-and-storage/nvidia-rtx-spark-laptops-go-on-sale-with-blackwell-superchip)

- First half of next year, and the first half of the year after: mass-production targets for the two new 3nm lines TSMC is adding at Fab 18 in Tainan.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Second Arizona fab volume production begins third-quarter twenty twenty-seven, advancing US three-nanometer supply.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC's second Arizona fab is slated for volume production in the third quarter of 2027, slightly ahead of the previous schedule, which moves US three-nanometer supply forward. Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said on the October 15 call that the shell is built and tools are moving in. A Chinese startup also showed a laser-produced-plasma EUV source it rates above 15 watts, and Samsung put a near-term start on a second Taylor fab.

### Top Story
On the October 15 earnings call, TSMC chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said construction of the second North Phoenix fab is complete and the site is in tool move-in and installation. He set volume production for the third quarter of 2027, slightly ahead of the previous schedule. That second fab is the three-nanometer plant. The first Arizona fab has been operating since 2024 on four-nanometer. Early construction has also begun on a fourth fabrication plant and on TSMC Arizona's first advanced packaging facility. Source: [azbigmedia.com](https://azbigmedia.com/business/tsmc-arizona-accelerates-production-timeline-as-earnings-soar/)

### Silicon
**Giga Computing servers carry Scaleway's new AMD Instinct cloud: HPCwire**
Giga Computing, a Gigabyte subsidiary, said it is supplying the servers for Scaleway AI and cloud services built on AMD Instinct GPUs, unveiled at ai-PULSE in Paris. The multi-rack deployment uses Gigabyte G4L3-ZX1-LAT4 direct-liquid-cooling servers, each with eight AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and two AMD EPYC 9005 CPUs. Each MI355X is specified with 288 gigabytes of HBM3E, on the open ROCm software stack. Motul supplies closed-loop direct liquid cooling, Bull handles cluster testing and deployment, and VAST Data supplies the data platform. Scaleway is offering the capacity as EU-jurisdiction cloud under the Cloud Sovereignty Framework. Chief operating officer Albane Bruyas said Giga's experience with high-density, liquid-cooled servers is particularly valuable at this scale. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/giga-computing-powers-scaleways-new-amd-instinct-gpu-services-to-accelerate-ai-workloads/)

**Samsung Foundry's photonic-wafer plan, as reported from Seoul: SammyGuru**
SammyGuru, citing Korea's MTN, reports that Samsung Foundry plans to enter the photonic integrated-circuit market on 12-inch, 300-millimeter wafers. The first step described is selling wafers, with a later expansion into combining electrical ICs with photonic ICs and into optical packaging. Named targets include optical-module makers Coherent and Lumentum, plus fabless companies that design photonic ICs. MTN puts TSMC's COUPE optical-packaging platform roughly one to two years ahead, and cites advanced-packaging market shares of 72.5 percent for TSMC and 5.9 percent for Samsung. GlobalFoundries, UMC, and Tower are also in silicon photonics, the same report says. Source: [sammyguru.com](https://sammyguru.com/samsung-silicon-photonics-acquisition-tsmc/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Ericsson and partners launch Sferical One in Sweden: HPCwire**
HPCwire reports that the sovereign AI supercomputer Sferical One was officially launched this week in Sweden. Ericsson is among the Swedish companies that have started to use it. Founding members of the Sferical AI initiative are Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB, and Wallenberg Investments. SKF is a strategic partner. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/ericsson-and-partners-launch-sferical-one-ai-supercomputer-in-sweden/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Samsung's second Taylor fab is lined up for an early-November start: TechPowerUp**
At an October 15 event near the Taylor, Texas site, Jonathan Taylor of Samsung Austin Semiconductor said construction of Fab 2 should start early next month and that the building will be one and a half times bigger than Fab 1. TechPowerUp, citing DigiTimes and South Korea's The Guru, reports that Taylor Fab 2 will span roughly 2.7 million square feet, with mass production targeted for 2030. Tesla's 16.5 billion dollar agreement runs through 2033 and covers the AI6 chip, and Samsung is also set to build Tesla's AI5 on two-nanometer in Texas. Samsung plans to invest over 37 billion dollars across Central Texas, backed by up to 4.745 billion dollars in CHIPS Act funding. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353801/samsung-to-break-ground-on-second-taylor-fab-in-november-production-targeted-for-2030)

**Langdao Silex shows a homegrown EUV laser source: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp reports that Chinese startup Langdao Silex has demonstrated FlintNano LPP-OXXO, which it presents as the first homegrown extreme-ultraviolet laser source. The company says the system delivers over 15 watts of EUV output and uses components that are about 90 percent domestically sourced or developed. Published specifications list a 1,000-watt driving laser at repetition rates between 1 and 20 kilohertz, conversion efficiency above 2 percent, and continuous operation of more than 100 hours. The prototype is described as suitable for wafer exposure testing, with further tuning still required. ASML has never shipped an EUV scanner to China; the Dutch government, under US pressure, blocked those exports in 2019, while ASML continues to ship DUV systems to Chinese customers. A light source is one subsystem of a scanner; the rest is reflective optics, wafer positioning, and integration across the machine. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353808/chinese-startup-unveils-first-homegrown-euv-laser-source)

### The Teardown: When the Film Has to Survive the Hole
A stacked package only prints if the wafer under the lens is flat enough that the next pattern lands on the last one. That alignment is overlay. Bow is the warp that film stress puts into the wafer: the surface leaves the focal plane, and features shift sideways from the grid the scanner is trying to hit. EE Times, reporting Zeiss Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology at SEMICON West, quotes US sales head Raghu Nayak calling wafer flatness a huge issue, and describes Zeiss DUNE as a tool that measures topography and corrects it wafer by wafer so the next fabrication step can still overlay.

The same account puts a second job beside that correction. Zeiss NLX is specified for 300-millimeter wafers. It is built to make internal structures in a modern package visible without destroying the package, so connections between stacked dies can be checked and a defect caught before the wafer is scrapped. DUNE tries to put the surface back where the scanner expects it. NLX asks whether the bonds inside the stack are actually there. Those are sequential gates, not substitutes: a flat wafer can still hide an open bond, and a bond map does not flatten the wafer the scanner is about to expose.

Panel-level packaging changes the shape of the substrate the film has to cover. EE Times reports that Von Ardenne is extending its deposition portfolio from the 300-millimeter wafer to panel-level packaging, and that US chief executive Stephen Strausser told the magazine the company has a one- to two-year lead in coating and deposition for panel-level glass substrates. The process named is HiPIMS, high-power impulse magnetron sputtering, aimed at high-aspect-ratio barrier and seed layers inside through-glass vias. Those vias are holes through a glass panel that later take metal so a redistribution layer can land on a pad. The claim EE Times relays is dense, highly adherent film in those holes, so a deposition recipe already running on 300-millimeter wafers can move to a larger panel, including through-glass vias and redistribution layers.

The figures in that account are the format and the lead, and they are enough to see where time sits. NLX's inspection field is the 300-millimeter wafer. Von Ardenne's stated lead is one to two years, and the migration it describes is away from that same 300-millimeter format onto a panel. A panel is the larger form factor, so each coating pass addresses more package area than a 300-millimeter disc, but only if the film stays continuous down a hole whose depth is large relative to its width. That continuity is the whole engineering content of the high-aspect-ratio claim here. One to two years is the gap Strausser claims over other coaters on panel-level glass. A packaging line that wants a second source of that barrier-and-seed step is waiting on that interval, not on a lithography node announcement.

The stage is a separate limit, and EE Times puts it on the same show floor. Heidenhain unveiled the METIS HP, a full air-bearing planar platform for the most demanding step-and-scan work, including direct laser writing and high-resolution optical inspection. The company supplies sub-nanometer motion control and position feedback for wafer manufacturing. An air bearing takes mechanical contact out of the loop that has to hold position while the tool steps. Sub-nanometer is the scale the article gives for that feedback. Overlay fails when the stage and the bowed wafer disagree by enough to miss the last layer; DUNE is trying to remove the wafer's share of that miss, and the air bearing is trying to remove the stage's.

SEMICON West 2026 ran October 13 to 15 at Moscone Center in San Francisco. SEMI chief executive Ajit Manocha opened it by calling semiconductors a trillion-dollar industry. Beside the metrology, EE Times notes equipment installer ABM, after its merger with WGNSTAR, pointing at a technical training center in Boise, Idaho, with room for about 500 participants a year. Five hundred people a year is a training throughput. It only binds if the tools above ship into fabs that need installers who can keep a sub-nanometer stage and a glass-via coater inside the process window those tools were sold on.

DUNE is the correction that matches a round wafer whose defect is bow: measure this wafer, flatten this wafer, send it back into a 300-millimeter flow. That choice stops matching the package when the interconnect leaves the wafer and enters a glass panel. The clock then is Von Ardenne's one- to two-year lead on panel coating, because a wafer-flatness tool does not put barrier metal down a through-glass hole. NLX stays the inspection that matches the problem only while the defect is an internal open inside a 300-millimeter package. Once the yield loss sits on a panel, outside that wafer field, a wafer-format internal camera is aimed at the wrong object, and the 300-millimeter correction loop no longer bounds the part.

### On the Horizon
- Before the end of the decade, TSMC expects its third Arizona fab, the two-nanometer plant, to be fully operational.
- By the end of 2026, Samsung plans operations at Taylor Fab 1, which uses EUV for its two-nanometer process, with volume production in 2027.
- Samsung Foundry's reported entry into photonic IC wafers is aimed at next year.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Taiwan plans a Texas supplier park worth up to four billion dollars while tightening AI-chip export rules.**

**What You Need to Know:** Taiwan’s economics minister says the government plans a Texas industrial park worth up to four billion dollars for chip suppliers, in the same interview that sets criminal penalties for restricted AI-chip exports to China. On the show floor, an open AMD Helios switch tray shows why 224G in-rack copper still needs retimers. Finland’s grid rules, as described in Vienna this week, would put data centres under one megawatt ahead of larger builds.

### Top Story
Kung Ming-hsin, Taiwan’s Minister of Economic Affairs, told Bloomberg in an interview Asiae published Friday that Taipei will align some export-control measures with U.S. measures after commitments in the reciprocal trade agreement with the United States. The government plans to add AI servers and advanced semiconductors to the controlled-export list. Once those measures take effect, exporting restricted AI semiconductors to China will be a criminal offense under the Foreign Trade Act; today that export is not itself a criminal offense, so prosecutors use other laws. U.S. authorities have claimed that Nvidia products worth billions of dollars have been smuggled into China in recent years. The same interview reaffirmed a Texas industrial park worth up to $4 billion for suppliers working with Nvidia, TSMC and Foxconn, with loan guarantees and help on visas and land. Source: [asiae.co.kr](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026101616242905832)

### Silicon
**T-CREATE EXPERT Ai CQDIMM DDR5 Wins GOOD DESIGN AWARD 2026: TechPowerUp**
Team Group says its T-CREATE EXPERT Ai CQDIMM DDR5 desktop memory has won the GOOD DESIGN AWARD 2026. It is the company’s first DDR5 CQDIMM desktop module at 128 GB, aimed at creators running generative AI locally. An independent clock driver and patented IC grading verification give a default 8,000 MT/s at the JEDEC voltage of 1.1 V without overclocking. Two slots total 256 GB. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353783/team-group-t-create-expert-ai-cqdimm-ddr5-memory-wins-good-design-award-2026)

**Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA Extend the Automated-Driving Partnership: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA announced they will extend their strategic partnership for the next generation of driver assistance and automated driving. The work pairs Mercedes-Benz engineering and MB.OS with NVIDIA Hyperion’s in-vehicle compute and sensor architecture, the Alpamayo Stack driving software, and the Halos safety system. Halos adds a parallel safety stack with redundancy and guardrails. NVIDIA says the combination supports advanced driver assistance and future SAE Level 4 applications, including robolimousines. Board member Jörg Burzer called NVIDIA Mercedes-Benz’s most important strategic partner in automated driving. Mercedes-Benz also uses NVIDIA technology for vehicle engineering simulation and inside MO360, its digital production ecosystem. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/mercedes-benz-and-nvidia-expand-strategic-partnership-to-advance-safe-highly-automated-driving-in-the-next-decade)

### Data Centres & Power
**Workload Value Enters the Data-Centre Policy Argument: Data Center Knowledge**
Data Center Knowledge reports that workload value is still an emerging policy question, not a live permitting rule, after Informa’s Data Center Europe event in Vienna on October 13–15. Sandvine’s 2024 Global Internet Phenomena Report puts video streaming, social media and related applications from Meta, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Netflix at about 65 percent of internet volume. Goldman Sachs has projected that AI’s share of the overall data-centre market will double to 30 percent over the next two years. Branko Jovanović, speaking on a panel, pointed to Finnish grid-connection amendments that would prioritize data centres under 1 MW, which could favor smaller enterprise or research sites over larger AI, colocation or hyperscale builds without explicitly ranking workloads by social value. The article notes there have been no significant attempts yet to write those distinctions into approvals. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/regulations/could-the-societal-value-of-workloads-shape-data-center-policy-)

**Press-Connect Piping as a Cooling-Install Method: Data Center Dynamics**
In a sponsored Data Center Dynamics interview, Viega’s Stephen McAfee calls press technology the fastest way on the market to connect piping, against processes that can take hours. He ties cooling-loop reliability to five nines, about five minutes of downtime in a year. Welding or brazing is hot work: the space is isolated and other trades pause. On small-diameter pipe, he says welded joints fail more often, with X-rays showing cracks, porosity, inclusions or incomplete fusion, and a bad joint can force the system apart and back together. Contamination in secondary loops that feed processor cold plates can clog micro-fin vanes. Viega’s seal sits outside the flow line, so liquid does not contact a non-metallic surface; the same press systems are specified for chilled water, technical cooling loops, facility water and fuel. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/marketwatch/the-future-of-data-center-efficiency-starts-with-pipes/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Commerce Shifts $955 Million of a GlobalFoundries CHIPS Award: ExecutiveGov**
ExecutiveGov reports that the Commerce Department is shifting $955 million in a GlobalFoundries CHIPS award toward photonics and advanced packaging. Source: [executivegov.com](https://www.executivegov.com/articles/commerce-globalfoundries-chips-award-955m-advanced-packaging)

**GlobalFoundries and TSMC Add U.S. Silicon-Interposer Capacity: ET Datacenters**
ET Datacenters reports that GlobalFoundries and TSMC have partnered on U.S. silicon-interposer supply, with manufacturing capacity to be added at GlobalFoundries’ Malta, New York, facility. The five-year agreement supports TSMC’s CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem. Volume production for that advanced AI packaging begins ramping by the first half of 2028. Source: [datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ai-compute-infrastructure/globalfoundries-tsmc-partner-for-us-silicon-interposer-supply/134987486?utm_source)

### The Teardown: Why the Helios Switch Tray Still Needs a Retimer
Two Broadcom Tomahawk 6 switch chips, each rated 102.6T, sit side by side in a double-wide 1OU tray. ServeTheHome opened that tray on the HPE booth floor at OCP 2026. It is the HPE Juniper QFX5252, built as an AMD Helios switch tray, and the layout is the opposite of a chassis switch whose value is a wall of front-panel ports. The fabric connectors are at the back. They blind-mate into the rack’s cable cartridges. The electrical problem is the run from each switch chip to those connectors at the SerDes rate Helios actually uses.

That rate is 224G PAM4. The switch that sounds like the scale-up part is Tomahawk Ultra, and ServeTheHome spells out why it is not in this tray. The current Tomahawk Ultra is a 112G PAM4 SerDes switch: 512 lanes of PAM4-112G. A lane specified at 112G does not carry a 224G PAM4 signal, so those 512 lanes are not a Helios fabric. The tray uses Tomahawk 6 because Helios is on 224G PAM4 SerDes. Two of those 102.6T devices in a 1OU tray are why the assembly is liquid cooled. Internal manifolds feed the cold blocks on the chips.

The connectors do not sit next to the silicon. ServeTheHome notes that the cabled connections to the rear high-density fabric connectors are quite far from the Tomahawk 6 chips, and some are very far. The liquid-cooling blocks in that gap are retimers. A retimer takes a degraded high-speed waveform, samples it, and launches a clean edge so the next stretch of copper can still meet the eye opening the SerDes requires. At 224G PAM4 the channel budget is short enough that a long board-plus-cable run inside one rack fails unless something rebuilds the edge. AMD is using retimers for that reach. NVIDIA has worked to remove them. After the retimer, the tray still needs what ServeTheHome calls an enormous array of copper cables into the cartridges. Retimers buy the reach; copper still carries the lanes. That combination is the picture the site says it will use when explaining why co-packaged optics is the next simplification: move the optical engine next to the switch chip and the long electrical run goes away.

The cooling split matches the power split. The two switch chips and the retimer blocks are on liquid. Fans and airflow guides remain over heatsinks on other components. NVIDIA has been pushing fans out of the AI rack; this Helios tray still air-cools those other bits. The front latch levers are very long because the back panel is long, has to blind-mate, and the insertion force into the Helios rack is significant. ServeTheHome had already covered the QFX5252 at HPE Discover 2026. The show-floor difference is the assembled tray, built to scale up inside the rack rather than out of front-panel connectors.

The copper-plus-retimer choice stops being the right one when the cartridge connectors have to sit so far from the Tomahawk 6 that a 224G PAM4 lane only closes inside the rack if a retimer rebuilds the edge and a full copper array finishes the run. That is the condition already sitting in the open QFX5252: the retimers are there because the connectors are far, and co-packaged optics is the simplification once that distance is what in-rack copper cannot close on its own.

### On the Horizon
- EE Times lists a 30-minute BitCast on information-flow tracking for pre-silicon security sign-off at 8:00 a.m. PST, 11:00 a.m. EST and 17:00 CET.
- ET Datacenters says volume production for the GlobalFoundries–TSMC U.S. silicon-interposer supply begins ramping by the first half of 2028.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Twenty-four hours after install, a photonics quantum computer was already running customer work in London.**

**What You Need to Know:** Orca Computing's PT-3 photonics system was installed and operational within twenty-four hours at Digital Realty's LHR19 in London and is already powering two projects. TSMC followed a sixth record quarter with a fourth-quarter revenue guide of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. BrightRay has only a letter of intent for a 10 MW prefab hall in Indiana.

### Top Story
Orca Computing has deployed its PT-3 photonics quantum computer at Digital Realty's LHR19 data centre in London, and Data Center Dynamics reports the machine was installed and operational within 24 hours. It is already powering two projects. The deployment is a working system in a colocation hall, not a lab announcement of a future machine. Photonics is the computing approach Orca is running on that floor. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/photonics-quantum-firm-orca-computing-deploys-pt-3-system-at-digital-realtys-lhr19-data-center/)

### Silicon
**Agentic workloads pull the CPU back into the AI rack: Semiconductor Engineering**
Semiconductor Engineering reports that agentic workloads are raising CPU demand because an agent branches on model outputs, and that if-then-else work is what CPUs do while GPUs still run the models. Industry estimates cited in the piece put the CPU-to-GPU ratio moving from about 1:4 toward as low as 1:1. Arm's Satadal Bhattacharjee said CPU demand has risen, and Synopsys's Ron Lowman said the ratio has changed. Reasoning models, mixture-of-experts architectures, and reservoir computing still rely on GPUs; mixture-of-experts lets a query load fewer parameters. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/agentic-ai-alters-the-cpu-gpu-balance/)

**Open links, not one fabric, for the AI factory: Semiconductor Engineering**
A Semiconductor Engineering post argues there is no single architecture for training and inference, so designers are combining memory, compute, and connectivity instead of forcing every workload into one design. UCIe is described as a common die-to-die interface for an open chiplet ecosystem, so compute, I/O, and memory interfaces can share a package without one proprietary link. Across the wider system the piece names PCIe, CXL, UCIe, UALink, and Ethernet, with 224G SerDes as the high-speed signaling layer. Memory is split the same way: HBM4E and LPDDR6 are called out for different needs. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/building-ai-infrastructure-for-greater-choice-and-flexibility/)

### Data Centres & Power
**BrightRay looks to expand into US with 10MW prefab data center project in Indiana: Data Center Dynamics**
BrightRay's Indiana project is announced, not under construction and not energized: Data Center Dynamics reports a letter of intent with an unnamed US partner for a 10 MW prefab data centre. A letter of intent is not a build contract and not an energized site. The 10 MW figure is the capacity attached to that intent as BrightRay looks to expand into the United States. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/brightray-looks-to-expand-into-us-with-10mw-prefab-data-center-project-in-indiana/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**TSMC's fourth-quarter guide lands after a sixth record quarter: TIKR**
TSMC guided fourth-quarter revenue to $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, about 14% above the third quarter at the midpoint, after net profit rose 68.7% to NT$763.06 billion, about $23.55 billion. Third-quarter revenue was $46.72 billion, above the company's own guide of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion. C.C. Wei said 2026 dollar revenue should grow around 44%, and capex stays at $60 billion to $64 billion. High-performance computing was 68% of third-quarter revenue, and 2nm rose to 8% of wafer revenue from 3% in the second quarter. Gross margin was 66.4%, down from 67.7%, and CFO Wendell Huang said dilution from overseas fabs should run close to 2% this year and widen to 3% to 4% later. Source: [tikr.com](https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmc-posts-a-sixth-straight-record-quarter-and-its-q4-guide-says-the-ai-boom-isnt-slowing-heres-the-fuller-picture?ref)
Source: [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/tsmc-posts-record-profit-as-ai-chip-demand-defies-market-debt-fears/)

**TSMC will talk Terafab only if TSMC runs the fab: Yahoo Finance**
On the analyst call, C.C. Wei said TSMC is still discussing Elon Musk's Terafab and that the fab has got to be run by TSMC. Musk had said his companies would build and operate the facility themselves, and that TSMC might sublease part of the site but would not run manufacturing. Intel is reportedly helping Musk's companies develop the technology the plant would use. The Information reports TSMC will add a new 3nm fab as AI orders pile up, and a separate account says a Texas fab is under evaluation with no final decision. Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/elon-musk-invitation-tsmc-ceo-090518081.html)
Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/tsmc-add-new-3nm-fab-ai-orders-pile)

### The Teardown: Why the Weight File Sets the Memory Floor
An open-weight release puts the trained parameters where a buyer can load them onto hardware the buyer controls. Semiconductor Engineering's account of that shift starts from the memory those parameters occupy. Ashish Darbari, chief executive of Axiomise, notes in the piece that OpenAI reports gpt-oss-120b runs on a single 80 GB GPU and gpt-oss-20b can run on a device with 16 GB of memory, and that both use MXFP4 quantization. The weights are the file. The GPU or the smaller device is the shelf. If the file does not fit the shelf, that model does not run there, whatever else the chip can do at peak.

Sharad Chole, chief scientist and co-founder at Expedera, tells the same article that publishing the weights cuts vendor lock-in. The user can host the model or pick a service provider, and no single company owns the next token. He also dates the map. As of September 2026, he said, the larger open-weight models come primarily from outside the United States, from Europe or Asia, and the field is moving toward trillion-parameter models. Guillaume Boillet, vice president of strategic marketing at Arteris, draws the line the file does not cross: an open-weight release is not necessarily open source, because training data, code, and usage rights may remain restricted.

The worked example is the pair Darbari cites, and it should be read as a fit check rather than a benchmark. A model at the 120-billion-parameter scale, stored in MXFP4, is reported to fit one 80 GB GPU. A model at the 20-billion-parameter scale, in the same format, is reported to fit 16 GB. The article is explicit that memory fit alone does not establish useful performance. Architects, the piece says, still have to account for memory capacity, sustained performance, changing models, and deployment security. Chole's catalog count makes the churn concrete: about 250 open-weight models from major companies landed on Hugging Face in the last two years, not counting quantized variants or models from smaller firms. He describes an effort to distill a 400-billion-parameter DeepSeek-C model into an 8-billion-parameter Qwen model, and he cautions that the industry is not about to see 100-billion-parameter models breaking every device benchmark. Thomas Andersen, vice president for AI and machine learning at Synopsys, adds the domain limit: general-purpose models are strong on public text and code, and hardware design needs proprietary data those public weights do not contain. The article's own takeaway is the clock mismatch: model architectures can change in weeks, while silicon takes years.

The single-device fit stops being the right deployment when the job needs something the weight file does not carry, or when the memory that merely holds the weights cannot sustain the run. That missing piece is the training set, the source code, or the usage right Boillet flags. It is also the sustained-performance and long-context load listed beside raw capacity, and the proprietary design data Andersen says has to be added before the model is useful in a chip-design flow. At that point the 80 GB shelf that fit gpt-oss-120b is the wrong boundary. The machine has to be sized for the data and the duty cycle, not for the parameter count that cleared the first filter.

### On the Horizon
- Fourth quarter of 2026: TrendForce figures reported with TSMC's results put CoWoS capacity at a target of 120,000 wafers a month.
- End of 2027: that CoWoS target rises to 180,000 wafers a month, a 50% jump from the late-2026 figure.
- Through 2026: Nvidia is booked for 800,000 to 850,000 CoWoS wafers, more than half of TSMC's CoWoS output, on industry estimates reported by TrendForce.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Twenty times more AI compute by 2030 still stalls if memory cannot feed it.**

**What You Need to Know:** SK hynix told SEDEX 2026 that AI-infrastructure compute demand could reach about 20 times this year’s level by 2030, and that HBM alone will not hold the inference working set. The company is pushing High Bandwidth Flash and 3D-stacked DRAM as new tiers between today’s HBM and SSD. Specification work on HBF is aimed at January 2027.

### Top Story
SK hynix president Ahn Hyun, speaking at SEDEX 2026 in Seoul, said computing performance required for AI infrastructure could reach about 20 times this year’s level by 2030, and that raising the speed of a single memory device will not close the gap. Asiae reported his account of context length moving from about 128K tokens in 2024 to around 1 million, with a further path toward 100 million, so data spills from HBM and DRAM onto SSDs. High Bandwidth Flash stacks NAND with the through-silicon-via approach used for HBM; SK hynix is aiming for about half the bandwidth of same-generation HBM and more than 10 times the capacity, and it plans to finalize the specification next January after a July draft, with SanDisk and cloud providers including Google in the standards work. On 3D-stacked DRAM, which places DRAM on a GPU or NPU and ties it with TSVs, Money Today reported about 10 times the bandwidth of HBM and about half the power, while Asiae reported dozens of times more input/output pathways and a large cut in power. Ahn also described custom HBM with customer functions on the base die, CXL pooled memory, and storage whose input/output performance would rise four to eight times. At the booth, SK hynix showed an NVIDIA Vera Rubin superchip and an HBM wafer signed by Jensen Huang, plus a 64GB RDIMM on a 10-nanometer-class sixth-generation (1c) process, a 256GB 3DS RDIMM, and a 128GB MRDIMM. Source: [mk.co.kr](https://www.mk.co.kr/en/business/12175683) · [asiae.co.kr](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026101413163270120) · [mt.co.kr](https://www.mt.co.kr/en/industry/2026/10/14/2026101412241926278)

### Silicon
**Quadric’s GPNPU puts scalar, vector, and matrix on one ISA:** Semiconductor Engineering
Semiconductor Engineering carried Quadric’s account of a General-Purpose Neural Processor delivered as configurable IP: one instruction stream, one ISA, and a C++ and Python programming model covering scalar, vector, and matrix execution. The Chimera core pairs a scalar unit with a 2D SIMD processing-element array; each element has a 32-bit ALU, a configurable MAC bank, local register-file SRAM, and a neighbor-communication path. On-chip memory, both that local SRAM and L2, is software-managed rather than hardware-cached. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/generative-ai-on-a-general-purpose-neural-processor-gpnpu/)

**Bolt finishes a first test round on the Zeus physics chip:** HPCwire
HPCwire reported that Bolt Graphics completed a first round of testing on Zeus, a test chip aimed at hardware-accelerated physics modeling for HPC, digital-twin, and video-rendering work. The finished GPU is not expected to ship from TSMC until 2028. Bolt also opened an office in Taiwan. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/13/bolt-graphics-touts-hardware-accelerated-physics-modeling-on-zeus-test-chip/)

**Upscale AI launches Token Fabric for mixed accelerators:** HPCwire
HPCwire reported that Upscale AI launched Token Fabric so rival AI processors can work together in the same data centre. The problem it names is no longer a single-vendor GPU floor: cloud providers are building their own AI chips, and specialized accelerators are entering beside NVIDIA GPUs. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/13/upscale-ai-launches-token-fabric-to-make-rival-ai-chips-work-together/)

**OSS announces Tamarack-G, an OCP and VPX hybrid:** HPCwire
One Stop Systems announced Tamarack-G, a Modular Open Systems Approach platform that hybrids OCP and VPX for rugged enterprise-class compute. The company describes it for AI, machine learning, and sensor processing at the edge, and it is debuting at the Association of the United States Army meeting. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/oss-unveils-tamarack-g-a-next-gen-ocp-vpx-hybrid-system/)

**Cadence argues package sign-off has to start inside the layout tool:** Semiconductor Engineering
Semiconductor Engineering posted a Cadence methodology for early, iterative optimization of chiplet packages as CoWoS-R, CoWoS-L, high-bandwidth memory, and high-speed interfaces multiply signals. The paper’s claim is that importing those designs into a separate analysis tool, then looping redesigns, can blow the schedule, so in-design analysis and multiphysics engines have to run before late sign-off. It frames the stack against a conventional 2D system-on-a-chip, with TSV, wafer-level packaging, and 3D die or wafer stacking as the packaging menu. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/accelerating-advanced-ic-package-design-a-methodology-for-early-and-iterative-optimization-of-chiplet-integration/)

### Data Centres & Power
**NVIDIA puts $250 million of UK compute behind agentic safety research:** NVIDIA Newsroom
NVIDIA announced a five-year compute donation valued at $250 million, $50 million of access a year, for agentic safety and security research in the United Kingdom. Compute is to be delivered through UK-based NVIDIA Cloud Partners, with infrastructure hosted in the UK; provider selection, technical architecture, and commercial terms are still to be agreed. A proportion supports Oxford’s BOLD lab, UCL’s SOFAIR lab, and Imperial College London, alongside the wider UK research community. The commitment sits on top of existing work that includes the University of Bristol’s Isambard-AI supercomputer, powered by NVIDIA Grace Hopper Superchips. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-commits-250-million-to-advance-uk-agentic-safety-and-security-research-over-the-next-five-years) · [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/uk-ecosystem-deployment/)

**Fuse Energy moves household support AI onto its own B300 machines:** NVIDIA Blog
NVIDIA’s Europe roundup said Fuse Energy is moving customer AI off outside infrastructure and onto its own machines built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra. The deployment is described as serving more than 450,000 UK households. It is an in-house system move, not a named campus with a megawatt rating. Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/uk-ecosystem-deployment/)

**Amperesand aims solid-state transformers at AI power spikes:** EE Times
EE Times reported that Amperesand’s solid-state transformers are aimed at smoothing AI data-centre power spikes with batteries, 800-volt DC conversion, and microgrid control. The piece describes a power-electronics approach, not a named site, owner, or megawatt interconnection. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/amperesand-aims-to-smooth-ai-data-center-power-spikes/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Musk calls Micron’s memory pricing reasonable and some other quotes too high:** TradingKey
TradingKey, citing JPMorgan, reported that Micron has signed 26 long-term supply agreements covering more than 35 percent of projected revenue through 2030, with remaining performance obligations of about $150 billion, and that more than 75 percent of 2027 capacity is already committed, some agreements running through 2031. The same report said tight supply in HBM and server DRAM could persist until 2028. Musk has also said Tesla cut planned LPDDR5 on the AI5 chip from 144GB to 96GB, and planned LPDDR6 on the AI6 chip from 216GB to 144GB. Source: [tradingkey.com](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262215489-tsla-spacex-musk-spcx-mu-skhynix-hbm-ai-dram-tradingkey) · [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/1c03e478-5306-4690-a20b-1c5020db4635)

**ASML warns 2027 and 2028 tool plans fall short of demand:** Yahoo Finance
Yahoo Finance reported that ASML on Wednesday posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter net sales and revenue, reaffirmed its outlook for the full year, and warned that current supply plans for 2027 and 2028 are expected to fall short of outsized customer demand. That warning is about lithography-tool supply, not about a new process node. Source: [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tsmc-shares-rise-ahead-closely-054241637.html)

**ETEL launches the METIS HP air-bearing stage for step-and-scan tools:** Semiconductor Digest
ETEL introduced the METIS HP, a full air-bearing planar motion platform for demanding step-and-scan semiconductor applications, including direct laser writing and high-resolution optical inspection. Semiconductor Digest carried the launch. The stage is a tool-motion platform, not a wafer output figure. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/etel-launches-metis-hp-high-precision-motion-platform/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=etel-launches-metis-hp-high-precision-motion-platform)

### The Teardown: Why the Frame Stays in the Building
A city operations agent starts with a camera frame, a meter, and a file that already live in the building. NVIDIA’s blog on European city deployments describes the split. Cosmos open models and the Metropolis blueprint for video search and summarization look at the stream and name a condition: congestion, equipment state, an unused space, a safety hazard. Nemotron open models then reason over that result and answer in ordinary language. Omniverse libraries hold the twin, so a planner can try a change before the street does. The accelerators sit in what NVIDIA calls a locally operated AI factory, packaged by system builders including Cisco, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro. The design choice is not a faster chatbot. It is that the frame, the model, and the operations log do not have to leave the city’s control to be useful.

Take the Department of Côte-d’Or as the worked case, as NVIDIA’s blog tells it. Akila and ThinkDeep built operations agents that combine sensor data, infrastructure data, and historical data in a sovereign digital twin using Nemotron, Omniverse, and accelerated computing, with Cosmos adoption planned for the video. The estate is more than 500 public buildings. The agents cover energy, compliance, safety, and climate resilience. Document search time went from weeks to minutes. Total operating costs fell by 10 percent, with a target of 30 percent at scale. That is the local-factory arithmetic in one department: the same buildings, a shorter search, a stated cost cut, and a larger cut that is still a target rather than a result.

A second worked step is the clock on a citizen request, not a camera. In Italy’s Milan region, Galene.AI, Dell Technologies, and TD Synnex are deploying a locally operated AI factory, starting with Cinisello Balsamo and planning expansion to four additional municipalities. NVIDIA’s blog says the applications are meant to put municipal data in front of people in seconds versus hours, with local governance of the data kept in place. The four-municipality plan is still a plan. The seconds-versus-hours claim is the latency the local factory is supposed to buy: the record stays in the region, and the answer does not wait on a distant queue.

The condition that breaks the choice shows up when the camera has never seen the event the agent is asked to warn on. At the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, Milestone and Dell Technologies are testing agentic vision with Cosmos and the same video-search blueprint for oil-spill warnings, training on synthetic data because real incident footage is scarce. A local factory can score a frame it holds. It cannot invent a spill physics the harbor has not recorded and then treat that score as an operations order. The same break appears when the job is no longer “what is wrong in this building” but a training run or a cross-city simulation larger than the local accelerators. Ten percent off operating cost does not, by itself, pay for that larger machine, and the 30 percent figure is a scale target, not a measured result across the 500 buildings. When the question needs either a hazard the synthetic set has never stood in for, or more compute than the city’s own factory holds, the frame has to leave the building or the warning has to wait.

### On the Horizon
- SK hynix is targeting a finalized HBF specification in January 2027, after the July draft with partners.
- Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote is set for Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 11 a.m. CEST.
- Bolt Graphics does not expect the finished Zeus GPU to ship from TSMC until 2028.
- Smart City Expo World Congress runs November 3–5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA and partners are presenting city AI factories.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Maia 300's memory bandwidth rises two and a half times, so inference stops waiting on compute.**

**What You Need to Know:** Maia 300's memory bandwidth rises two and a half times versus Maia 200, to 18 terabytes per second, while FP4 compute rises about 37 percent. Microsoft says production deployments begin in 2027 and that it will scale Maia to multi-gigawatt deployments as its primary inference system. The chip is announced, not shipping: a 950-watt N2P part with 288 gigabytes of HBM4, 96 of them in a 167-kilowatt rack.

### Top Story
Microsoft announced Azure Maia 300, with production deployments beginning in 2027, and said it will scale the Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027 so Maia becomes the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services. StorageReview reports each accelerator pairs a TSMC N2P compute die with eight HBM4 stacks for 288 gigabytes at 18 terabytes per second inside a 950-watt TDP, and a rack holds 96 accelerators in a 167-kilowatt envelope, with 32 ports of 400-gigabit links. Maia 200 was a monolithic N3P die with six HBM3E stacks, 216 gigabytes and 7.1 terabytes per second; Maia 300 splits into a main compute die, two I/O dies and four memory dies. Peak compute is 13.8 POPS at FP4 and 6.9 POPS at FP8, up from 10.1 and 5.1 — about a 37 percent FP4 gain against a 2.5 times bandwidth gain, 33 percent more capacity, and about twice the HBM bandwidth per watt. Microsoft claims 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems and up to 7 times the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200. Maia 200 is already in production, including on Copilot, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by year-end; Maia 300 remains a 2027 production plan, not a shipped rack. Source: [blogs.microsoft.com](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/10/12/microsoft-to-expand-azure-maia-system-to-multi-gigawatt-deployments/) · [storagereview.com](https://www.storagereview.com/news/microsoft-maia-300-hbm4-n2p-chiplet-96-accelerator-rack) · [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/12/microsoft-boosts-hbm-bandwidth-by-2-5x-with-maia-300-accelerator/)

### Silicon
**CXMT plans a 4F² DDR5 server module by year-end: Global Times:** ChangXin Memory Technologies plans to launch a next-generation DDR5 RDIMM for servers on a 4F² DRAM architecture by the end of 2026, president Cao Kanyu said at an industry conference on October 10 in Shanghai. Each cell occupies four times the square of the minimum feature size, against the mainstream 6F² cell. TrendForce, citing MyDrivers, says that smaller footprint can raise density 30 to 50 percent in the same area. The approach uses a vertical surrounded-gate transistor to improve electrostatic control and cut leakage, and TechNode reports more than 300 patent families on the architecture plus work on hybrid bonding so the memory array and peripheral logic can be processed separately. This is a stated launch plan for a server module, not a part in volume shipment. Source: [globaltimes.cn](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202610/1371987.shtml) · [scmp.com](https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3370505/chinas-cxmt-unveils-key-progress-chip-structure-pursued-samsung-sk-hynix) · [trendforce.com](https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/10/12/news-cxmt-accelerates-4f%c2%b2-dram-push-eyes-year-end-server-ddr5-rdimm-launch/) · [technode.com](https://technode.com/2026/10/12/cxmt-plans-next-generation-ddr5-server-memory-using-denser-dram-architecture/)

**Lisa Su reveals 6th Gen EPYC Verano: AMD:** AMD says Lisa Su revealed 6th Gen EPYC “Verano” as the next step on its CPU roadmap for the AI era. The company describes the prior generation, EPYC “Venice,” as spanning GPU hosts, agent sandboxes and general-purpose compute. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2109792923684577368)

**Zeiss and ASML paper sets hyper-NA at 0.75 or above: Semiconductor Engineering:** Semiconductor Engineering’s October 13 paper roundup includes a Carl Zeiss SMT and ASML paper titled for a hyper-NA lithography system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75. The roundup lists the work; it does not add a throughput, dose or resolution figure for that system. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-technical-paper-roundup-oct-13-2/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Bull ties Angers to Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72, and Altair-1 reaches orbit on Jetson: NVIDIA:** NVIDIA says Bull is extending European AI server production to Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory, inaugurated Friday, October 2. Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation, launched this month and has reached orbit. Loft Orbital integrated the spacecraft; Orbitworks, a joint venture of Loft Orbital and Marlan Space, built it in Abu Dhabi. It flies NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit. The NVL72 line is a 2028 production plan; the satellite is in orbit. Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/france-ecosystem-agentic-computing/)

**AMD donates the Helion Agentic Rack to OCP: AMD:** AMD says it is donating the Helion Agentic Rack to the Open Compute Project to advance open AI infrastructure. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2109792214889185652)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Qnity ties growth to local-for-local materials: Nikkei Asia:** Qnity, a supplier of semiconductor chemicals and materials to TSMC and Intel, is placing plants near customers, including a facility in Taiwan. Its CEO says a local-for-local strategy, including sourcing more than 70 percent of raw materials inside each region where it operates, is how it grows as chipmakers shorten supply chains. Source: [asia.nikkei.com](https://asia.nikkei.com/editor-s-picks/interview/tsmc-intel-supplier-qnity-bets-on-local-production-to-win-business)

**Applied Materials unveils a $5 billion EPIC Center: Semiconductor Digest:** Applied Materials unveiled the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, described as a $5 billion investment and the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility. The notice is an unveiling of that R&D site, not a wafer-start or a tool-install count. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/applied-materials-unveils-5b-epic-center-in-silicon-valley/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=applied-materials-unveils-5b-epic-center-in-silicon-valley)

**ERS launches an automated 310 mm panel packaging tool: Semiconductor Digest:** ERS electronic announced a fully automated panel-level packaging system for 310 by 310 millimetre substrates. The item is a tool introduction, not a stated capacity or a customer line. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/ers-introduces-automated-310mm-panel-level-packaging-system/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=ers-introduces-automated-310mm-panel-level-packaging-system)

### The Teardown: Why a Hundred Wafers a Year Is Nobody’s Job
A packaging tool is paid for by the wafers that keep it busy, not by how clever the process is. Europe’s advanced-packaging trouble, as EE Times reports it from Fraunhofer IZM, starts after the prototype works. A company can need fan-out, through-silicon vias or some other nonstandard flow at tens, hundreds or thousands of units. That run is too long for a research institute to carry indefinitely and too short for a high-volume outsourced assembly and test house to staff.

Rolf Aschenbrenner, deputy director of the Fraunhofer Institute for Reliability and Microintegration, sees that gap as an access problem: volume too low for advanced packaging at a commercial OSAT, while the institute can do prototypes and, in some cases, small-volume builds. The intended path is to adapt the process, prove it, and transfer it. The transfer dies when no industrial line will take the book of business.

Fan-out wafer-level packaging makes the arithmetic plain. An RF customer might need around 100 wafers a year. For a large OSAT, Aschenbrenner’s account is that 100 wafers a year does not register, so the job is declined. A medical miniature-camera customer is smaller still: about 20 wafers a year. One wafer can hold tens of thousands of cameras, so those 20 wafers are the entire market, not a pilot that grows. Nobody else’s depreciation schedule is built for that book.

The same reporting covers detector arrays for a novel CT scanner. Sensors have to sit very close together. Conventional wire bonds open gaps that hurt the image, so the design routes connections through the silicon to the backside. The customer wanted that work done in Europe. A research line can hold the process. A production OSAT will not, unless the annual wafer count looks like utilization rather than a favour. The research-fab hold stops being the right home for the flow when an industrial packager will take that yearly wafer count as a real run — 20 wafers, or 100 — instead of a volume that never pays the tool.

### On the Horizon
- Production deployments of Maia 300, and multi-gigawatt Maia scale, are set for 2027, Microsoft says.
- Bull’s Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems are planned for 2028, with European trays and Angers rack integration.
- CXMT’s 4F² DDR5 RDIMM for servers is planned by the end of 2026.
